#884. Respect? Exposure? Why England's star names are going abroad

Anthony Gordon joined Barcelona from Newcastle in the summer

Bayern Munich's Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane, Real Madrid's Jude Bellingham, Barcelona's Anthony Gordon - three of England's star players, all of whom are playing their club football abroad.

The Premier League is widely regarded as the most competitive league in the world with the greatest financial muscle, but that does not always translate to the biggest individual profiles and, increasingly, star names are looking elsewhere.

Since Cristiano Ronaldo won the Ballon d'Or in 2008, for example, only Rodri in 2024 was playing in England at the time of being crowned the best player in the world. Michael Owen, in 2001, was the last Englishman to do so while in England.

The trend of English players going abroad has gathered pace since a teenage Jadon Sancho signed for Borussia Dortmund in 2017 and that is reflected in this current Three Lions squad - seven of the initial 25 play outside England.

"Jude Bellingham and Harry Kane were decisive for us in the World Cup and I see no reason they won't be in the future," said England boss Thomas Tuchel when talking about his big stars playing outside of their home country.

"It's good that Anthony has stepped up now. He is the third one. There is obviously a relevance to them playing abroad but I don't see that a player who plays in the Premier League cannot step up and be decisive for us."

At the World Cup in the summer and during the last international break, however, it was those three players' goals and assists that proved decisive.

Currently there are 43 English players on the Football Association's radar playing their club football in Europe.

The FA's technical director John McDermott believes it is a "huge positive" to have so many players playing across Europe.

"I spoke to a couple of the boys that are playing abroad at the moment," he told BBC Sport. "The exposure they get in those leagues, playing Champions League or European football, where you're not necessarily having to bang out 55 games, but you still have got time to do your weight training and your gym work.

"Often if you're playing in the English competition or in the EFL, where it's 46 games - you know it's game, game, game, which is fantastic - but for some players that opportunity to get the training in-between and to practise developing on technique or other areas, there's benefits to that."

McDermott was previously at Tottenham Hotspur and says that even when he was in club football, he was a "big believer" in players going abroad to "develop character" and "independence".

"I think being in another changing room and learning another language just puts you under the pressure to adapt," he added.

"And I think for any young person that ability not only to become technically, tactically more adept, but also culturally have to pick up something else - it's huge and prevents people from becoming complacent or just getting used to the same old, same old."

Gordon said in the recent international break he feels he gets more respect now he plays for one of Europe's elite sides, compared with when he was at Newcastle.

"I think he's always been respected," McDermott said.

"I remember when Trips (Kieran Trippier) came back, and Trips was a good player, but when he came back from Atletico (Madrid) I noticed he was just maybe tighter technically and noticed there was a change that Kieran came back with.

"So I'm not sure if he's respected more ... but I think you want all of the players - whether they stay in England [or not] - every six months you see this sort of incremental step where they've added something, another dimension to the game.

"That can sometimes come in this country, obviously, playing with different players, being in new competitions, but I think going abroad definitely helps that.

"And I've seen that with Anthony already and some of the other boys. They come back, it's four months since you've seen them and there's another dimension there."

McDermott is keen to make clear that developing in England can still be of a huge benefit and that Jarell Quansah and Jobe Bellingham, two of England's squad who are now playing in Germany, also played in the EFL.

"There's all different ways, I don't think there's this elixir, I don't think there's this magic formula, 'this is the way'," McDermott said.

England reached the semi-finals of the World Cup for just the third time in their history in the summer.

McDermott was asked if he thought now the Three Lions had more players abroad, it could help develop England's style or performance in major tournaments.

"Yeah, possibly. Again don't underestimate if you're playing now in the Champions League at an English club," he said.

"We would like more players in the pipeline. I think at the moment we're on about 26% or 27% English-qualified players playing the Premier League.

"We've got 40 to 50 players playing at Champions League quality and playing in European football, top Premier League clubs, so let's not underestimate our own product."

McDermott says it is clear the impact having players in different countries is having on the squad, but it is then down to the manager to blend the style.

"I think the different cultural experiences they get, the different exposure they get to play in different types of football is fantastic.

"But still, the England manager has got to try and find that singular blend when they come back of the English players, the Spanish players, the German players, the Italian players, it's all sort of an eclectic mix that they're bringing."

England's record goalscorer, appearance maker and captain Harry Kane is playing his club football in Germany with Bayern Munich, while Jude Bellingham has never played in the Premier League - leaving Birmingham for Borussia Dortmund and now Real Madrid

Gordon has impressed since making his move to Barcelona in the summer with three goals and five assists in 15 appearances in all competitions.

The 25-year-old is regularly lining up with some of the best players in the world, in a front line alongside Lamine Yamal and Raphinha.

The lure of European giants like Real Madrid, Barcelona and Bayern Munich is hard for any player to turn down.

Arsenal's approach for Vinicius Jr this summer was always going to be hard to complete as the famous white shirt and lifestyle in Madrid is, for most players, the pinnacle.

But does moving abroad to one of Europe's top clubs also alter people's perceptions of English players?

"I always felt in England, people respected me because I was fast and I pressed, but they never actually respected the quality and IQ that I play with," Gordon said in a recent interview with ITV.

"Only the players I play with ever seem to notice that. I think now I'm at Barcelona and I play a different style, those qualities are highlighted much more and people are actually starting to take notice that I'm not just quick."

Gordon produced some standout moments in the World Cup, assisting both of Kane's goals in the last-32 win over DR Congo, winning a penalty in England's last-16 win over Mexico and scoring the goal to put England ahead in the semi-final against Argentina.

Captain Kane said the winger is "showing that he belongs at the highest level, for Barcelona and England" and that Gordon is "relishing" being one of England's "main men".

"I think it's great," added England and Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin. "The fact that we've got top-level English players playing abroad now at top European clubs, I think it's only good for English football and us as a national team.

"You see they bring different experiences that they're learning from overseas and they bring it into this group and I think as you can see they're only growing in confidence and as players and I think it's only a positive thing."

#883. Aberdeen appoint Liechtenstein's Frick as head coach

Mario Frick has been announced as the new head coach of Aberdeen, taking over from the sacked Stephen Robinson to become the club's fourth manager in 2026.

Capped 125 times as a striker for Liechtenstein, the 52-year-old was last in charge at Luzern, leaving the Swiss club in the summer after five years.

He follows Robinson, Peter Leven and Jimmy Thelin in leading the side in this calendar year and will take charge for the first time against Scottish Premiership bottom side Kilmarnock on Saturday.

"Throughout our discussions, he demonstrated a clear vision, strong leadership qualities and a deep understanding of what is required to build a successful team," said Pittodrie chief executive Adrian Bevington.

"He was also exceptionally well regarded by the many people across the game we consulted during the process, and the board was unanimous in its belief that he is the right person to lead Aberdeen forward."

Former Motherwell and St Mirren boss Robinson was dismissed on 9 November, with Aberdeen second bottom of the table and having lost four games in a row in all competitions.

'Aberdeen hunt yet another manager after ill-fated Robinson reign'

Latest Aberdeen news, analysis and fan views

Watch new Aberdeen boss Frick score against Scotland in September 2010

Frick, who also managed Vaduz in the Swiss Super League, will be assisted by Roman Matter and is the seventh permanent manager since Dave Cormack took control of the club in November 2019.

As a player, his former clubs include FC Basel, FC Zurich, St. Gallen and Grasshopper, while his 16 international goals make him Liechtenstein's all-time top scorer.

"Mario is a strong personality with clear ideas about how he wants his teams to play," added sporting director Lutz Pfannenstiel. "He brings energy, ambition and a winning mentality, and knows how to build a strong team environment.

"We were looking for the right person to lead the next chapter of Aberdeen FC, and I'm convinced Mario has the qualities, character and vision to make a real impact."

Frick got Vaduz promoted in 2020 before helping Luzern avoid relegation following his move there in 2021.

The next again year he guided them to a fourth-placed finish and European qualification, although they were knocked out of Conference League qualifying by Lee Johnson's Hibernian.

Aberdeen say Frick "has built a strong reputation for transforming teams, handing top-flight debuts to more than 30 academy players during his coaching career".

Hibs striker Thibault Klidje and current Aberdeen goalkeeper Marius Muller both played under him.

Aberdeen did not disclose contract details for Frick as he takes over a side with just three wins from 12 Premiership outings this season.

One of his international goals came at Hampden Park in 2010 when a late Stephen McManus header rescued a 2-1 win for Scotland.

Matt: Terrible appointment. Not exactly a glowing CV. Will be out the door in 12 months or less.

Ian: Left field but it is a bold decision. Let us get back up we we belong.

Kev: Could be good. Could be bad. If it is the latter the the Dons will be in real trouble. It's a very quick appointment...

Sandra: Never heard of him but kudos to the club for acting in a timely manner for once. All the best Mario, you'll need it.

Malky: A curve ball if ever there was one. I admit I was unaware of him; I had to Google him. As far as I'm aware he has a 37% win ratio, so he'll fit right into the current state this club finds itself in. I hope to be proved wrong, but for me it's underwhelming.

Harry: He certainly can't be any worse than the last few that have come and gone. Surely gonna hit the jackpot at some point.

#881. Cast your vote for BBC Women's Footballer of the Year 2026

Meet the BBC Women's Footballer of the Year contenders

Voting is now open for the BBC World Service Women's Footballer of the Year 2026.

Fans worldwide can vote from the five-player shortlist of Temwa Chawinga, Ewa Pajor, Alexia Putellas, Alessia Russo and Khadija 'Bunny' Shaw.

The vote closes on Wednesday, 18 November at 09:00 GMT.

For the first time in the award's history, the winner will be announced as part of the BBC's Sports Personality of the Year on Sunday, 13 December as well as on the BBC World Service and the BBC Sport website and app.

Contenders for the award - now in its 12th year - are nominated by coaches, journalists and former professionals. It covers the period September 2025-August 2026.

Cast your vote, and read more on the five contenders.

Sorry, this vote cannot be loaded. In order to vote you need to enable JavaScript in your browser.

Listen: Who is your BBC Women's Footballer of the Year 2026?

BBC Women's Footballer of the Year contender Temwa Chawinga

Chawinga has established herself as one of the world's most prolific forwards.

Her impact on the National Women's Soccer League is clear. Her extraordinary form helped Kansas City Current clinch the NWSL Shield as the league's top team in the regular season.

Chawinga scored 15 goals in the 2025 season as she became the first player to be named NWSL MVP in back-to-back campaigns. She also won the Golden Boot for the second year in a row.

Those performances earned her a contract extension through until 2029.

Chawinga returned to international football with Malawi for the 2026 Women's Africa Cup of Nations.

Alongside her sister Tabitha, she helped Malawi reach the country's first Wafcon final and - in doing so - qualify for the Women's World Cup for the first time.

Chawinga scored against Nigeria, Egypt, Ghana and Algeria at Wafcon, winning the tournament's Golden Boot with five goals.

BBC Women's Footballer of the Year contender Ewa Pajor

Pajor is widely regarded as a world-class number nine - and it's clear why.

Instrumental as Barcelona won four trophies last season, Pajor scored their first two goals in a 4-0 Champions League final victory over Lyon.

The goals meant she finished as the competition's top scorer, while the result meant she won the Champions League for the first time after losing in five finals - four with Wolfsburg and one with Barcelona.

Pajor also enjoyed an outstanding second season with Barcelona in Liga F, scoring 16 league goals in her 23 appearances and providing five assists. She was a key player as Barca won the domestic treble.

On the international stage, Pajor captains Poland and is the team's leading goalscorer.

BBC Women's Footballer of the Year contender Alexia Putellas

Club: London City Lionesses Position: Midfielder

Putellas showed again this year why she is one of the most influential footballers in the world.

After 14 years with Barcelona, she delivered a spectacular final season with the club - helping them win four major trophies.

Her 14 goal contributions in 11 Champions League appearances helped her childhood club win the competition for the fourth time, and she remained a decisive figure bringing experience and leadership when it mattered most.

Putellas delayed announcing her move to London City Lionesses to avoid creating a distraction, but in July 2026 she completed that transfer, saying the club's "women-only identity and ambition" were important factors.

Internationally, Putellas was instrumental in Spain retaining the Women's Nations League in late 2025, scoring three goals against Sweden in the semi-finals before being named player of the finals as Spain defeated Germany 3â0.

Last month she was awarded a record-equalling third Ballon d'Or.

BBC Women's Footballer of the Year contender Alessia Russo

Russo has proven to once again be a trusted and integral attacking force for Arsenal, while remaining a key player for England.

She scored 13 WSL goals last season to finish second in the league's scoring charts, and also added six assists in her 22 appearances. In total, she registered 24 goals and eight assists across all competitions.

Among the highlights of her season was winning the inaugural Women's Champions Cup with Arsenal, beating Corinthians 3- 2 after extra time.

It was the first competitive trophy Arsenal's women's team had lifted at the Emirates, though they finished runners-up to Manchester City in the WSL.

Russo remains a first-choice striker for England and in April scored her 30th senior international goal to move into the top 10 of Lionesses goalscorers.

She was also nominated for the PFA Player of the Year award.

BBC Women's Footballer of the Year contender Khadija Shaw

After a fine year, Shaw has positioned herself as one of the world's elite forwards.

The defining striker in Manchester City's Women Super League title-winning campaign, she scored 21 goals in 22 league appearances, won a record third consecutive WSL Golden Boot and was named WSL Player of the Season.

Her goals were central to City ending a 10-year wait for the league title.

They went on to complete the Double, with Shaw scoring the opening goal in their FA Cup final victory over Brighton at Wembley to finish the season with 26 goals in all competitions.

She also reached a major personal milestone in December 2025 when she became the first player in the history of City's professional women's team to score 100 goals.

Amid uncertainty over her future, Shaw announced at City's end-of-season celebrations that she had signed a new four-year contract through to 2030.

#879. Tenerife return to action after death of De Miguel

Tenefire fans display a banner paying tribute to Jesus de Miguel

Tenerife played their first game since the death of striker Jesus de Miguel on an emotional day at the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium.

De Miguel died at the age of 30 on 3 November, a day after colliding with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a home match in Spain's Segunda Division.

Tenerife beat bottom side Ceuta 2-0 on Sunday, with tributes to De Miguel paid both before and during the game.

Lengthy standing ovations preceded and followed a minute of silence before the match.

In the ninth minute play was stopped and a round of applause took place, while a video of De Miguel was shown in the stadium, as happened at all first- and second-tier games in Spain last weekend.

Tenerife fans displayed a banner that read: "Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternally blue and white."

Forward Nacho Gil opened the scoring for the home side in the 40th minute and celebrated by holding up De Miguel's shirt.

Gil revealed a message written under his shirt that read: "Demi, always in our hearts."

Neal Viereck scored four minutes from time as Tenerife ended a run of six games without a win. They are 14th in the table.

Tenerife's game with Granada on 7 November was postponed and the club invited fans to the stadium to pay their respects to De Miguel.

Owono was given a 12-match suspension by the Spanish football federation for the challenge which resulted in De Miguel's death.

The federation has ruled that the game between Tenerife and Andorra, which was abandoned seven minutes into stoppage time after the incident occurred, will not be replayed and the 2-2 score will stand.

#877. Phil Collins Walks With 2 Canes During Rare Public Appearance

Phil Collins made his first major public appearance in months at the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame on Nov. 14, using the assistance of two canes during the evening.

The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame marked another day in paradise for Phil Collins fans.

After all, the beloved rocker made an ultra-rare public appearance for the Nov. 14 induction ceremony in Los Angeles, marking his first major event since May amid his ongoing health challenges.

For the occasion—which saw Collins inducted as a solo member, having previously been included as part of Genesis 2010—the 75-year-old walked the carpet in an elegant black suit which he paired with a white button-down shirt, the collar of which he left loose, and with the assistance of two wooden canes.

Collins was joined for the evening by three of his five children; Joely Collins, 54, whom he shares with ex-wife Andrea Bertorelli; Lily Collins, 37, whom he shares with ex-wife Jill Tavelman; and Nicholas Collins, 25, whom he shares with ex-wife Orianne Cevey. (The drummer is also dad to Simon Collins, 50, with Bertorelli and Matthew Collins, 22, with Cevey.)

In fact, during his speech on stage, Collins proved there will always be gratitude in his heart for his former wives, reserving a special shoutout for them.

"They loved me through the years, but more importantly, they have given me five great children," he said, per USA Today. "They are incredibly talented, and I made life tough for them growing up. But they have turned into such wonderful human beings. I love them to death."

The “Son of Man” artist—who in recent years has been navigating challenges with his kidneys, nerves and spine, in addition to type-2 diabetes—also took a moment to address his health after first taking to the stage.

“Thank you so much, I'm really not as bad as it looks," he told the audience, holding his canes aloft. "I'm much better."

And he thanked his longtime assistant Lindsay Evans for helping his health get back on track.

"Without her, I wouldn't be here. I'd be in a box, six feet under," he noted, saying Lindsay was able to show him his lifestyle choices were "bad, and she showed me what to do to make it better."

As for his musical legacy, Collins is still thanking his lucky stars for everything that has come his way.

"I've really been just very, very lucky," he said. " I grew up just wanting to play the drums. That's all I wanted to do. Everything else has been a very happy accident."

And when it comes to his future, and whether that includes a return to the stage, Collins teased there might be something in the air for fans.

“You haven't heard the last of me," he noted, "I can promise you that.”

For more stars who have spoken about their health challenges publicly, read on.

The Blink-182 drummer stopped smoking weed after being diagnosed with "precancer of the esophagus."

"I loved blunts and I would smoke too much," he shared on a November 2026 episode of the Big Bro with Kid Cudi podcast, recalling how his doctor said it was a "serious case. "He’s like, ‘This is your warning shot. Don’t f--l around. You’ve got to stop smoking."

The Jessie alum opened up about her "hellish" migraines, sharing how they've worsened after suffering five concussions over the course of her life.

"The brain injuries make things significantly worse," Ryan shared during a September 2026 episode of Mythical Kitchen’s Last Meals. "I had a pretty crazy, life-altering brain injury a few years ago, and I was out of commission for six months."

While Ryan described her first four concussions as "incidents," she said her fifth one was trauma caused by "sustained shaking over a minute of time."

Now, the former Disney Channel star needs to close her eyes to "think better."

"Quite often the world is really loud. It’s really too bright. There’s a lot going on," she explained. "The visual data that I'm taking in can be so distracting and so loud. Then, with the migraines—which are significantly worsened by that—it sort of is too much."

Brianna "Chickenfry" LaPaglia's Ovarian Cyst

In May 2026, the BFFs podcaster underwent emergency surgery after doctors discovered a large ovarian cyst that had been twisting her organs and causing internal bleeding.

"There was a half a liter of blood in my pelvic floor," Brianna shared in a TikTok video after the operation. "I have five incisions all over my stomach. They went in through my belly button with a camera so they could find all the blood."

The Total Bellas alum revealed that one of her breast implants shifted after an elbow slam from fellow WWE star Piper Niven during a July 2025 wrestling match.

"It's OK," she told sister Bella Garcia at the time. "We're going to get it fixed one day. I told the doctor, I go, 'Newly divorced, so the minute the boots are hung up, I'm going to come back to you and we're going to make these girls look real good, because these girls are going to get some action in the future and that can't look like that.'"

In October 2026, the former The Bachelorette star detailed how she cracked a vertebra in her spine after setting her vibration plate—a motorized platform that rapidly moves back and forth to promote muscle activation and circulation—to "level 30, supersonic speed."

"Seemingly, subtly, somewhere on the way to 30, maybe 10 or 20, my vertebrae turn crooked and rub against each other," Windey shared in a Substack essaye aptly titled "Broke back, no mountain."

"It was too fast vibrations I guess, and too many vibrations maybe, and too much pressure to shake," she continued. "And it broke. Broke right off, like your ex-boyfriend’s bumper. Well, technically, it cracked."

The injury left her with what she described as "insatiable" paresthesia—a medical term for a tingling, pins-and-needles sensation.

"This is the greatest sense of condemnation; of persecution, I’ll ever feel," she added. "And I do wish it on my worst enemy If only they hadn’t wished it on me first."

The 12 Years a Slave star was diagnosed with uterine fibroids—non-cancerous growths that develop in or around the uterus—in 2014, the same year she won an Oscar for performance in the movie.

However, it wasn't until 2025 when she disclosed her diagnosis, writing on Instagram that she had been "suffering in silence" for more than a decade.

"When we reach puberty, we're taught periods mean pain, and that pain is simply part of being a woman," she shared. "We're struggling alone with something that affects us most."

The Beverly Hills, 90210 alum revealed in April 2025 that he was recovering from surgery after his appendix nearly burst.

“Last week, I started feeling some pain in my stomach,” Brian said in an Instagram video at the time. “I ended up going to the emergency room, and I had a perforated appendix. Not quite burst, but just before.”

He added, “I'm on the road to recovery. It's not an easy process. This is my first major surgery.”

In July 2025, the Daisy Jones & The Six star shared that she had been hospitalized due to a hernia—a gap in the muscular wall that's commonly found in the abdomen or groin area—caused by wearing tight pants.

"'Suki you never tweet anymore,'" she wrote on X, formerly known as Twitter. "Have you ever considered I wore pants so tight 6 months ago it caused a hernia & I’ve been too scared to tell you?"

Savannah DeMelo's Mid-Game "Medical Emergency" Mid-Game

The Racing Louisville midfielder collapsed just a few minutes into her soccer team's September 2025 match against Seattle Reign at Lumen Field in Seatle.

The United States Women’s National Team player could be seen slowly sitting down on the field with a teammate by her side, per Reuters, as the referee called for trainers to check her out. She collapsed seconds later.

“Savannah received immediate on-field care from medical personnel and was transported to a local hospital for further evaluation,” the National Women’s Soccer League wrote on X later that night. “She is stable and alert."

Adam Devine's Long-Term Injury From Childhood Accident

Adam Devine shared that injuries he sustained after getting hit by a cement truck when he was 11 years old are still affecting him to this day.

“It’s been a nightmare,” Devine said in a 2025 episode of the In Depth With Graham Bensinger podcast. “I have spasms all over. For a while, [the doctors] told me I was dying—literally, within this last year.”

He noted that pain comes and goes, adding, "My body has all these things that are a little wonky and a little wrong with it."

The Bachelor Nation alum shared that he went to the hospital “crawling on all fours” due to overwhelming back pain that was aggravated during an RV trip with a friend.

“Right now, knees to my toes, it’s, like, still tingly, which is crazy,” he said on a March 2025 episode of his Trading Secrets podcast. “And to put in perspective, I don’t know, man, like not to sound douchey, but like two, three weeks ago, maybe a month ago, I was squatting probably like 295 pounds. And right now, I can’t do a squat on my foot. I can’t do a one legged squat, I fall. It’s like I had a stroke or something.”

But with the help of a back specialist and some steroids, he added, “We’re on the mend.”

Real Housewives of Orange County’s Gina Kirschenheiter shared her ex-husband Matt Kirschenheiter suffered a heart attack in March 2025, but thankfully survived the ordeal.

The 30 Rock star suffered a health scare at a New York Knicks basketball game in March 2025, leading to him being wheeled out of Madison Square Garden.

However, the comedian shared an update on social media the following day, noting it was a case of food poisoning and that he was on the mend.

The Even Stevens alum shared in February 2025 that she was shot in the face while on a trip to shoot clay pigeons to celebrate husband Brendan Rooney's birthday.

"There was another party with us and they unsafely fired in the wrong direction and shot me in the face," she wrote on Instagram. "@thebrendanrooney immediately sprung into action, assessed me, and rushed me to the hospital. I was hit in 5 places, one was less than an inch from hitting me directly in my right eye."

The Kim Possible alum continued, "Unfortunately a fragment got lodged behind my eye and it is too risky to remove surgically at this time. Doctors will continue to monitor me (I can see normally at the moment)."

The actress said she was grateful to be alive. "I love my daughters, husband, family, and friends so much," she said. "I saw my life flash before my eyes and I’m telling you, hug the people around you every chance you can. Life can change in an instant."

While the internet isn't always a kind place, Amy Schumer is happy that, in this case, it helped her get answers."The internet really came for me after doing a bunch of press, and I was like, 'OK everybody, relax,'" Amy recalled of her "puffier" face on a January 2025 episode of Call Her Daddy. "But then doctors were chiming in in the comments and they were like, 'No no, we think something’s really up. Your face looks so crazy that we think something’s up. And I’m like, ‘Wait, I’m getting trolled by doctors?’"After these doctors said they thought she had Cushing syndrome and that it may be caused by spiking coritsol levels or steroid injections, the Life & Beth creator thought, "Wait, I have been getting steroid injections in my scars.""I had a breast reduction, a C-section, whatever, and so I was getting these steroid injections," Amy said. "So it gave me this thing called Cushing syndrome, which I wouldn’t have known if the internet hadn’t come for me so hard."Toda, Amy is just relieved she's OK. As she shared in a February 2024 News Not Noise newsletter, "Finding out I have the kind of Cushing that will just work itself out and I'm healthy was the greatest news imaginable."

Casey Fitzgerald's Neck Injury From Hockey Skate Blade

The AHL player was cut by a fellow player's skate during a game in December 2024 and received 25 stitches. His father, New Jersey Devils general manager Tom Fitzgerald later told ESPN after his son was fully recovered, "We're very lucky. I don't wish that on any parent."

Hailey Bieber had the "scariest moment" of her life when she was having breakfast with husband Justin Bieber and started experiencing stroke-like symptoms in March 2022."Justin was like, 'Are you OK?'" the Rhode skincare mogul shared a month later on YouTube, "and I just didn't respond because I wasn't sure. And then he asked me again and when I went to respond, I couldn't speak. The right side of my face started drooping. I couldn't get a sentence out."While Hailey said the facial drooping stopped and her speech came back, she went to the hospital to make sure she was OK."They did some scans and they were able to see that I had suffered a small blood clot to my brain," the model added, "which they labeled and categorized as something called a TIA [Transient Ischemic Attack]."Later, Hailey went to the University of California, Los Angeles, where she found out she had a hole in her heart called a patent foramen ovale (PFO).She explained the blood clot had traveled into her heart, "escaped" through the hole and went to her brain, leading to the TIA.Hailey said she had a successful PFO closure procedure and was now feeling great.

The same year Hailey had her health scare, Justin experienced one of his own.In June 2022, the "Baby" singer shared he was diagnosed with Ramsay Hunt syndrome, a condition that caused temporary paralysis to parts of his face and forced him to cancel the remainder of his Justice World Tour."It is from this virus that attacks the nerve in my ear and my facial nerves and has caused my face to have paralysis," Justin explained in an Instagram video at the time. "As you can see, this eye is not blinking. I can't smile on this side of my face. This nostril will not move. So, there's full paralysis on this side of my face."In fact, he told his followers it had gotten "progressively harder to eat." But after a while, the paralysis went away."He's doing really well," Hailey said on a June 2022 episode of Good Morning America, later adding, "He's feeling a lot better. Obviously, it was just a very scary and random situation to happen, but he's going to be totally OK and I'm just grateful that he's fine."

While Jamie Foxx initially kept details of his April 2023 hospitalization private, he later opened up about what he went through.One day in Atlanta, "I was having such a bad headache, so I asked my boy, I said, ‘Listen, I need an aspirin,’” the Oscar winner said in his 2024 Netflix special What Had Happened Was... “Before I could get the Aspirin, I went out. I don’t remember 20 days.”Jamie said he was initially taken to a doctor who gave him a cortisone shot and then sent him home. However, his concerned sister Deidra Dixon then drove him to a hospital, where they got an answer: He had a brain bleed that led to a stroke.Twenty days after undergoing an operation, the Django Unchained woke up May 4 in a wheelchair and couldn’t walk. He then went to Chicago for rehabilitation and therapy."All I can tell you is that I appreciate every prayer,” he said, “because I needed every prayer.”

Tracey Yukich's Medical Emergency on The Biggest Loser

The reality star revealed that she "died" while running a mile during the first challenge of the NBC competition series.

“I don't remember a lot,” she explained on Fit for TV: The Reality of The Biggest Loser. “I remember hearing the helicopter. I just felt like I was floating. And then my grandpa was there. And then I saw darkness. But then I saw light. So I knew, I knew I died that day.”

“My organs were literally shutting down,” she continued. “I didn't realize that I had rhabdomyolysis. And rhabdomyolysis is your body's way of saying, ‘I'm going to shut down on you.’”

Emilia Clarke filmed battle scenes for Game of Thrones, but in 2019, she published an essay in The New Yorker titled "A Battle for My Life."Having a bad headache at the gym, "I reached the toilet, sank to my knees, and proceeded to be violently, voluminously ill," the actress wrote. "Meanwhile, the pain—shooting, stabbing, constricting pain—was getting worse. At some level, I knew what was happening: my brain was damaged."She was taken to the hospital for a brain scan."The diagnosis was quick and ominous: a subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), a life-threatening type of stroke, caused by bleeding into the space surrounding the brain," the Emmy nominee added. "I’d had an aneurysm, an arterial rupture."Emilia had immediate surgery to seal the aneurysm, calling the pain "unbearable." While she was recovering, she continued, she experienced aphasia and was "muttering nonsense."A week later, "the aphasia passed," Emilia added, and she left the hospital a month after being admitted. At a 2013 brain scan, she learned a growth "doubled in size" and that she needed surgery again."When they woke me, I was screaming in pain," she wrote. "The procedure had failed. I had a massive bleed and the doctors made it plain that my chances of surviving were precarious if they didn’t operate again. This time they needed to access my brain in the old-fashioned way—through my skull."Thankfully, Emilia shared, she's now "at a hundred per cent."

Snoop Dogg's daughter Cori Broadus is grateful for her family.Because after she suffered a "severe stroke" in January 2024, her loved ones rushed to be by her side."I texted them that I just had a stroke and sent them a picture," she told E! News correspondent Will Marfuggi in December 2024. "Everybody just came to my rescue."Because of other medical concerns, Cori ended up staying in the hospital longer than she initially expected."I could have went home after my stroke, but my lupus wasn't doing so well," the Snoop's Fatherhood: Cori and Wayne's Story star continued. "My kidneys were failing. It was a lot going on."Today, Cori is on the mend."I'm doing great," she added. "I just had a little bit of motor skills that I had to work back on. But other than that, I was fine."

Shailene Woodley’s early 20s were not an easy time health-wise.“It got to the point where I was losing my hearing. I couldn’t walk for longer than five minutes at a time without having to lay down for hours, and hours and sleep. Everything I ate hurt my stomach,” the actress said on a September 2024 episode of the SHE MD Podcast. “It was this conflation of issues and diagnoses and different doctors telling me different things.”So Shailene—who chose to keep the exact condition private—set out to find answers. “I come from a very holistic background and study herbalism,” she added. “So I was very keen on, ‘I’m going to work with real MDs, [and] I’m also going to work with independent kind of healers.’ Just trying to search for some sense of comfort in my own skin.”It was a long journey—one that lasted for 10 years.“Throughout that decade, a lot of other things came from feeling so much discomfort physically,” the Big Little Lies star noted, “which was, ‘My gosh, if everything I eat hurts my stomach, I’m now suddenly afraid of food.’ And then going into the kind of mental f--ckery that can happen with that of body dysmorphia and confusion about identity and feeling safe in my own capsule, in my own skin, what that meant, and what that should be.”After tending to both her physical and mental health, Shailene is feeling much better.“It was a journey that ultimately physically resolved itself, and I am very healthy,” she shared. “I’m so happy to be able to say that."

#869. Why Northern Ireland won't focus on point they need in Hungary

A draw in Hungary on Tuesday would secure promotion to Nations League A for Northern Ireland

Still the only side in the 2026-27 Nations League yet to concede a goal, Northern Ireland know that one more clean sheet will be enough to secure back-to-back promotions.

After Saturday's 1-0 victory over Ukraine in Belfast, a draw away to Hungary in Budapest on Tuesday night would ensure Michael O'Neill's team top their group and advance to League A for the first time.

With three wins and two draws from their five games played, the visitors to the Puskas Arena are in the box seat in Group B2, but they will travel targeting victory rather than the draw that would suffice.

"We try and win every single game. If you don't, there's no point going," said veteran striker Josh Magennis, who will win a 95th cap should he feature.

"It's a weird [situation], but Michael's already told us that we're going to be set up to win.

"To have that in your back pocket is obviously nice, and the onus is going to be on them, but we're going to win it as much as them."

Watch on BBC iPlayer and BBC One NI from19:15 GMT; Listen on BBC Sounds and BBC Radio Ulster; Watch, listen, live text and clips on BBC Sport app & website

Northern Ireland were in a similar situation in the Nations League two years ago, albeit in the third tier, when needing a point away against Luxembourg to secure promotion.

They flew out of the blocks and raced into a 2-0 lead, only to allow a Luxembourg comeback in the second half, resulting in a nervy finish for a 2-2 draw.

Shea Charles was captain that night in November 2024 and believes the squad have taken a lesson from their loss of control in the fixture.

"I think we would have learnt from that time," said the Fulham midfielder.

"We were really comfortable in the game and let it slip a little bit.

"But we still came away with the draw and that's all that we needed. I'm really looking forward to it and I think we can go there and put in a good performance."

Charles echoed Magennis' sentiment that the permutations around the result will not alter the way the side approach the game.

He said: "I think we'll still try and go there and win. We know it's going to be a challenge, a very good team and a big crowd, I assume. It'll be tough.

"We've got to go out there and play the way we've been playing."

Sixteen years after his international debut, Magennis is the longest-serving player in O'Neill's squad and the sole survivor from Northern Ireland's only previous win in Budapest.

An unused substitute in the 2-1 victory that kicked off their successful Euro 2016 qualifying campaign, Magennis believes the squad's changing profile over the years has set them up well to target all three points.

"I've played in a lot of Northern Ireland teams where we've been very reactive to the opposition, trying to nullify them, but this is the type of group where we're able to overpower and overrun games and they'll have to think about us," he said.

Coming into this campaign, Northern Ireland's ability to grind out results beyond Windsor Park had been called into question.

Wins away to Georgia and Ukraine already in this campaign have changed that perception, and Magennis feels Hungary - one point behind Northern Ireland - will know the visitors are not to be underestimated.

"If they don't show us the respect that we deserve, then it'll be at their own peril, and they'll learn the hard way come 90 minutes when we take the three points," added the Stevenage striker.

"If they don't account for our running power, our physicality, our set-pieces, all that type of stuff, then that's down to them.

"We only play the team that's in front of us, but we'll go into it fully [prepared]."

#868. Michael J. Fox Steps Out With All 3 Daughters for Rare Family Outing

Michael J. Fox and Tracy Pollan’s daughters Aquinnah, Schuyler and Esmé joined their parents for the Michael J. Fox Foundation’s annual gala, marking a rare family outing.

Where Michael J. Fox is going, he just needs his family’s love.

The Back to the Future star was not only joined by his wife Tracy Pollan for the Michael J. Fox Foundation’s A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to Cure Parkinson’s gala on Nov. 14, but also by three extra special guests.

When Fox and Pollan stepped out at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City for the fundraising event, they were accompanied by 31-year-old twins Aquinnah and Schuyler, as well as 25-year-old Esmé. The three girls each wore elegant gowns and big smiles as they posed on the event’s red carpet alongside their parents. (Fox and Pollan are also parents to 37-year-old son Sam, who was not in attendance.)

Pollan, for her part, donned a calf-length black shift dress and heels, while Fox wore a black blazer over a navy t-shirt and black slacks.

The gala featured performances from John Mayer and Brad Paisley, as well as comedy sets from Josh Johnson and Tom Papa, while actor Denis Leary helmed the night as emcee.

Fox started the Michael J. Fox Foundation in 2000, nine years after he was diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease. In the time since, the organization has become an important player in the fight to cure the disease—with the annual gala acting as a way to thank the many hands who make executing the mission light work.

As Pollan told People at the event, “It celebrates everybody who’s worked with us for 20-plus years. Just the huge and amazing amount of money that’s been raised that goes directly into the scientists’ pockets, and they can just do all the work that’s necessary [to finding a cure]. We really are seeing so much progress.”

The 66-year-old also shared insight into how she and her family navigate Fox’s health challenges.

“I think you just have to do it day by day,” she reflected. “You have to look at what’s in front of you, and you have to stay in the moment.”

As for Fox, the Shrinking star has been candid about how grateful he is for his family walking beside him on his health journey.

In fact, when the 65-year-old accepted the Bob Hope Humanitarian Award at the 2026 Emmys, he specifically thanked his wife and kids “for their sacrifices, for their patience, and for their love.”

#867. Chapecoense air crash survivor wins promotion in final game

Alan Ruschel signed for Juventude in 2023

Alan Ruschel, a survivor of the 2016 plane crash that was carrying the Chapecoense football team, won promotion to Brazil's Serie A in his final game before retirement.

Ruschel, 37, was one of just six survivors when the plane crashed in Colombia and killed 71 people, including 19 of the club's players and the coaching staff.

Despite severe injuries and spinal surgery, Ruschel returned to football a year later and retires after earning promotion to Brazil's top flight with Juventude, his boyhood club which he re-joined in 2023.

Ruschel came off the bench in the 74th minute to help see out a 2-0 win over Botafogo, resulting in an emotional farewell with a lap of honour at the club's Alfredo Jaconi Stadium.

Before the game, he was also carried into the stadium on the shoulders of fans.

"I arrived here in 2007 with the club in Serie A and I am leaving the club there as well," Ruschel told a Brazilian television station after the match.

"My body wasn't responding any more. I had two consecutive knee surgeries, so I was starting to fighting with my own body.

"It wasn't working any more, even though being on the pitch was always a pleasure."

Ruschel referenced the plane crash in a video on social media which he posted the day before the game to confirm his retirement.

"Football has given me wonderful moments, but life has put me in front of challenges that I never imagined. November 29, 2016, a day that changed my life forever.

"I lost friends, companions and people with whom I shared dreams and projects.

"And God gave me a second chance. I didn't know if I would be able to play football again, but I believed that if I was here, there was still a purpose for my life.

"And today, I have the privilege of being able to choose the moment to say goodbye."

There were contrasting fortunes for Ruschel's former club, however, with Juventude effectively replacing Chapecoense in Serie A following their relegation after just one season in the top flight.

The club will return to Serie B having won just four games out of 34 during the season.

#866. Gypsy Rose Blanchard Slams Claims She Was Involved in Ken Urker Death

Gypsy Rose Blanchard reacted to the allegations she was somehow involved in the October death of her partner Ken Urker: “No other person had my heart like he did.”

Gypsy Rose Blanchard is navigating heartbreak.

And while she mourns the death of her partner Ken Urker—with whom she shared 2-year-old daughter Aurora—the Life After Lockup star is blocking out the noise that implies she played any sort of role in his passing, which she says was the result of an overdose.

When asked outright if she was involved with his death, Blanchard told 60 Minutes Australia, “Absolutely not. No.”

She shared that such allegations were “disgusting to hear, because that was the love of my life. That’s the father of my child,” adding, “No other man, no other person had my heart like he did.”

Nevertheless, she admitted that their relationship—which was first kindled briefly in 2018 and 2019, then found footing again in 2024 after Blanchard’s divorce from Ryan Anderson—had met challenges in the time following her release from prison.

“When I first came out of prison, everyone seemed to be so excited for me and my newfound freedom. And then over time, unfortunately, more criticism came my way,” the 35-year-old explained. “It was like things were fine in the home, we were happy. But online, there was so much negativity.”

And this isn’t the first time Blanchard referenced the challenges Urker faced from his life with her. In the days following his Oct. 1 death, Blanchard said her partner had “endured an unimaginable level of public scrutiny and relentless cyberbullying” leading up to his death.

“The cruelty toward him was something no human should have to endure,” she added in the Instagram Story. “I believe the tremendous weight of that scrutiny and harassment had a profound impact on him.”

Now, just over a month later, Blanchard still finds herself at a loss for how to move forward.

“Honestly, I’m still trying to process everything,” she said to 60 Minutes. “It’s been really difficult because, I just, I can’t make sense of anything anymore.”

“We had a plan for everything,” she added of Urker. “And everything was gonna be okay because he was right by my side. I wouldn’t have to do it alone. And now that’s changed, and I feel lost.”

She is, however, trying to redirect her heartbreak into good, sharing her efforts to enact new anti-cyberbullying laws in Urker’s name.

“Instead of lashing out at these people, I needed to do something more constructive with my anger,” she said. “So, I tried thinking in my mind, ‘What needs to change?’”

And to those who made hurtful comments towards Urker, she noted, “Imagine that being your boyfriend, your husband, your wife. And imagine that that was done to them and you lost them and they're gone forever. That’s what you did to us and that's your cross to bear.”

For a look back at Blanchard and Urker’s romance, read on.

Gypsy Rose Blanchard told E! News she knew Ken Urker was the one "probably the day I met him back in 2017."At the time, she was serving a 10-year prison sentence after pleading guilty to second-degree murder for her role in the 2015 killing of her mom Clauddine "Dee Dee" Blanchard.

The couple, who got engaged in 2018, even managed to create a festive atmosphere while Blanchard was incarcerated.

They split up in 2019 but, as Blanchard later noted, fate would come back to find them...

While Blanchard went on to tie the knot with teacher Ryan Anderson in 2022, she filed for divorce after less than two years of marriage. She and Urker Ken reunited in the spring of 2024.

"We are together and in a wonderful place in our relationship," she told TMZ that April. "We know it is going to be a long road ahead but are excited for the future."

Cloudy skies couldn't put a damper on the rekindled pair's mood.

Blanchard cuddled up next to Urker in this selfie snapped after their reunion.

Whatever he said had Blanchard beaming in a video about their "love story."

Blanchard shared a collage of some of her and Urker's most adorable moments a few weeks before revealing her pregnancy with their first child together.

At the time, she noted that their baby was due in January 2025.

The two found out they were expecting a baby girl during a sex reveal party in August 2024.

Before they become a family of three, Blanchard and Urker dined at a table for two during a September 2024 date night.

The parents-to-be took a trip to California, including Marina Del Rey, that October.

And while Blanchard noted on Instagram the view of San Francisco's Golden Gate Bridge was "incredible," she added, "the company made it unforgettable."

The duo sported their shades in this sunny snap.

On December 28, 2024, exactly one year after Blanchard was released from prison, she and Urker welcomed their daughter Auora.

Blanchard and Urker rang in their little girl's first birthday in 2025 with a Ms. Rachel-themed party.

#864. Club's first match since player's death abandoned because of serious injury

Hendon posted a picture on social media of defender Ethan Creary in hospital

A match involving a team playing for the first time since the death of one of their players was abandoned because of a serious injury.

Non-league Hendon were returning to action for the first time since midfielder Ezekiel Williams, 26, died in hospital on 2 November from head injuries after an incident in Milton Keynes.

Saturday's game at Bedfont Sports in the Isthmian League South Central Division was abandoned within 10 minutes after Hendon defender Ethan Creary was carried off on a stretcher and taken to hospital.

A Hendon statement read: "Early signs are that he's suffered a double break to the collarbone, possible shoulder ligament damage and concussion."

Hendon posted a picture of Creary, external in hospital wearing his kit with a message from the player.

"I have to be in the ward for 24 hours to assess any potential bleed in the brain. It's just protocol and I woke up feeling OK," Creary said.

Before Saturday's game, players from Hendon and Bedfont Sports observed a minute's silence for Williams.

The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County's Salomé Andrea—who is pregnant with her and Aaron Brimhall's third baby—addressed speculation that her husband has been unfaithful to her.

Salomé Andrea is setting the record straight.

After the Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County star shared insight into her marital issues with husband Aaron Brimhall on the Hulu series, she addressed speculation that he cheated on her while they were still married before their reconciliation following their 2025 breakup.

ICYMI, a scene in episode 4 showed Salomé—who shares 8-year-old twins Luca and Rue with Aaron—confronting her husband over comments she received on her May Instagram post, in which she announced she was pregnant with the couple’s third baby.

“This 20-whatever-year-old comes out saying, ‘Oh, he was sleeping with me while they were still married,’” the influencer told Aaron, who replied, “It happened once, and I was drunk. So, you know how you get any time I tell you the smallest little thing. I want to communicate with you and talk, but you’re just too abrasive.”

After a fan shared the clip from the show on Instagram Nov. 14, a user chimed in, writing in the comments, “I can't telllll you I cheated on you cuz you get wayyyy to[o] upset....yeah ....he's gross.”

Salomé, however, was quick to shut down the rumor, writing in response, “He never cheated on me just be to clear.”

#862. Why 'inspiring' Van Gaal influences Scotland head coach Pocognoli

Sebastien Pocognoli played for Louis van Gaal at AZ Alkmaar

Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli says he draws on the influence of legendary manager Louis van Gaal in his own coaching career.

The Belgian played under the Dutchman during their time at AZ Alkmaar, a special period for Pocognoli during which he won the Eredivisie title in 2009.

Van Gaal also previously took charge of the Netherlands, and now that he has moved into international football himself, the Scotland boss reflected on the 75-year-old's influence.

"I take a lot from all of my gaffers, but probably he was the one with the most experience," Pocognoli told BBC Scotland.

"I was very young and you know in that moment he had all the Barcelona young players between his hands, also Ajax players.

"The way that he treats the young players in a direct way, honest way and hard way was for me really inspiring in my daily job now.

"I was lucky to have a lot of good coaches but he was probably the most that impressed me day by day, and I felt progress under him.

"That I think is the best thing for players as a feeling."

Progress is exactly what every Scotland fan is yearning for. Under Steve Clarke, the amount of that very commodity plateaued.

Years in the international wilderness were expelled with two European Championships and a World Cup appearance, but they were punctuated by disappointing results and dour tactics.

Pocognoli's arrival signified not only a new era, but a new approach, formation, selection and outlook.

It has been far from straightforward for the Belgian as he approaches 100 days in charge next week. Five games, two wins over North Macedonia, a draw in Slovenia and two humbling defeats mark his tenure so far.

Within it, a fresh system and injection of different faces to offer a break from the norm, but also plenty signs that a transformation will not be an immediate reality.

Scotland's failings in front of goal has remained, while it is clear the Scots are still getting to grips with a back three, albeit with enforced changes in personnel.

"Everything in life takes time to build if you want to achieve something," said Pocognoli.

Scotland to play with bravery and courage - Pocognoli

You are Scotland boss Pocognoli - what would you do?

Six goals to go - will McGinn catch Dalglish & Law?

"So we know that in the performance world everything goes faster and quicker, but we have an objective and we know that we have to go through the up and down and the good moments. At the end I hope that all this experience can make us stronger.

"I don't ask the players to be patient, it's just to believe in what we are doing."

Pocognoli acknowledges he's not had much opportunity to immerse himself in Scottish culture after taking his first foray into international management.

A wander around Glasgow is about all he's managed. And any further exploring will have to wait until after Monday's Nations League test in St Gallen.

Finishing in the top two of their group seems a tall order for Scotland, who are requiring a win and snookers in Slovenia. It seems progression to the next Euros will instead roll on to the qualifying campaign next year.

"We don't have the control of what will happen because Slovenia will decide," Pocognoli said. "But if we want to have a chance to go through to the group stage and to go to the play-offs we have to go with the bravery and try to play with courage and try to force something.

"I don't believe that we are waiting for something then it will happen, so let's go through our quality and try to be aggressive and wait what happens in Slovenia."
