#827. Homophobia on the rise in football - what is your club doing about it?

Rainbow laces were a common sight for several years across football and other sports

Warning: this article contains offensive language

Homophobia and transphobia are on the rise in English football, with new data revealing record numbers of discrimination reports in the game - so what is the Premier League doing about it?

Last season, with little fanfare, the league introduced a new LGBTQ+ celebratory activation in February, Premier League With Pride.

The lowkey launch contrasts with the landscape of a few years ago, when England internationals like Jordan Henderson and Conor Coady were proudly proclaiming their allyship.

"The one thing it [Premier League With Pride last season] was lacking was engagement from players," said Jon Holmes, founder and lead of news organisation and campaign group Sports Media LGBT+.

"Not only would you have the rainbow armbands, but clearer allyship from players - that was more around the late 2010s. That has been in decline."

A report last month from anti-discrimination charity Kick It Out says they received a new high of 1,744 discrimination reports during the 2025-26 season, a 25% increase on the previous campaign. In this, reports of homophobia rose 46% to 203.

Kick It Out said it had received 142 reports of discriminatory mass chanting during the season, a 41% increase on 2024-25 and the highest number recorded. These reports included increases in homophobic and transphobic chants.

A prime example is the 'rent boy' chant predominantly aimed at Chelsea players and fans, for which incidents had dropped since it was criminalised in 2022. However, the combined 24 reports of homophobic chanting in 2025-26 season were the most in three years.

According to Kick It Out,, external many of the incidents over the past few seasons can be linked to domestic and world events, such as the Supreme Court ruling on gender leading to the FA's ban on transgender women in the women's game, which it says led to a spike in transphobic abuse.

The first Premier League With Pride event included rainbow branding at grounds - but nothing involving players

BBC Sport asked all 20 Premier League clubs what diversity policies they have regarding the LGBTQ+ community, and how much of their budget is dedicated to such schemes.

Nine clubs responded to the BBC request. None said how much money they invest in these areas.

A Nottingham Forest spokesperson told BBC Sport: "The club commits significant funding to this important area, and has an Equality, Diversity and Inclusion lead whose role is dedicated to ensuring inclusion is at the heart of everything we do."

Some clubs do visibly engage with their local LGBTQ+ community. Leeds United have been a sponsor of the city's Pride celebrations since 2018. Luke Ayling, then Leeds captain, marched in the Pride parade in 2022.

Liverpool and Brighton are annually represented in their city's extensive Pride events, as are the Manchester clubs.

Manchester City host an annual Progress flag-raising ceremony, while Manchester United said staff marched in the city centre parade. They also ran a flag competition with LGBTQ+ supporters' club Rainbow Devils, with the winning design displayed at Old Trafford for all matchdays.

Tottenham said that at the start of 2024, Spurs in the Community helped launch a weekly football session for members of the LGBTQ+ community.

And for the first time this season, all 20 current Premier League clubs have dedicated fan groups for LGBTQ+ supporters.

"It feels like there is a renaissance in the LGBT fan movement," said Holmes. "There is a rise in homophobia, but it does seem like the authorities are sitting up and taking notice. We can feel a degree of optimism."

But it is difficult for Premier League teams to encourage LGBTQ+ allyship and diversity, when representation within clubs is a mixed bag at best.

According to Kick It Out, which gathered data on the senior management teams from 17 out of the 20 current Premier League clubs, just 0.3% of people in those roles openly identify as LGBTQ+ - well below the UK population average according to latest national census data, with 4% of the British population identifying as LGBTQ+.

At a senior coaching level, from 11 clubs which responded there is no-one from the LGBTQ+ community.

Kick It Out says, comparing the dataset to relevant census data, that if football's workforce was truly representative of local communities, over 100 more people from the LGBTQ+ community would have to be employed at Premier League clubs.

The Premier League previously had a high profile association with LGBTQ+ charity Stonewall's Rainbow Laces campaign - but this was ended before the 2025-26 season

Rainbow Laces started in 2014-15 as a collaboration between Stonewall, Paddy Power and the Premier League. For two game weeks, usually around the end of November, players would wear rainbow-coloured laces or armbands, and the colourful branding would be seen in grounds and on broadcast idents.

Holmes said by the end it was doing more harm than good.

"I think the novelty of Rainbow Laces wore off," he told BBC Sport. "It also became more newsworthy to talk about the controversies; it became more difficult for players to engage without difficult questions.

"Also, club media departments are more risk averse, given growing toxicity on social media.

"It has been misconstrued that players were forced to engage, I think it was because Rainbow Laces became de rigueur, and it was perceived that captains would need to lead with the armband and allyship."

Rainbow armbands were introduced in 2017 for captains, having first been worn by MLS club Orlando City following the mass shooting at Pulse, an LGBTQ+ nightclub, in the city in 2016.

But the Premier League held its final Rainbow Laces campaign from 29 November to 5 December, 2024, and it was surrounded by controversy.

Marc Guehi, then Crystal Palace captain, wrote 'I Love Jesus' on his armband in what was widely viewed as a protest against wearing the armband (which was not mandatory).

Ipswich captain Sam Morsy refused to wear the armband, while Manchester United scrapped plans for a Rainbow Laces-themed jacket during the pre-match ceremonies following an objection by Noussair Mazraoui.

Simon Blake, CEO of Stonewall, admitted to BBC Sport that by the end of its 12-year lifespan in the Premier League, Rainbow Laces in that form had run its course.

"When it started, getting a few people to wear the laces was success," he said. "When it ended, when a few people didn't wear them there was criticism.

"If a campaign no longer has a positive vibe, perhaps it is time to do something different.

"Everything must evolve and change, but visibility still matters, it is important not to throw the baby out with the bathwater."

Stonewall held its first ever Rainbow Laces Day on 8 October this year, to encourage LGBTQ+ people to engage with sport. It had no connection with the Premier League.

Marc Guehi and Crystal Palace did not face any action after he wrote on his rainbow armband

It is notable that the players most ardently against Rainbow Laces were also vocal in their religious beliefs.

Guehi has spoken of the importance in his life of his faith and was one of several devout Christian players in the Crystal Palace dressing room. Both Morsy and Mazraoui are practicing Muslims.

Both Holmes and Blake acknowledge that this may have had an impact on Rainbow Laces.

"The influence of religion is clearly quite significant, but I think more understanding is coming in too," said Holmes.

"We have seen many parts of life less willing to engage with Pride, and football reflects that. The nature of LGBT campaigns is peaks and troughs, and we are in a trough."

"We don't have any specific data about what people's beliefs and views are, but we are in a world where people have different views, even within religions themselves," added Blake.

"The important thing is about behaviours, and we must learn to live with people who have these different beliefs and respect them.

"I don't want to speculate, as it would be too easy to assume people of faith would not be inclusive, I know from my work across 30 years that is not true; I have worked with many religious people who are LGBTQ+ supportive. Freedom of belief is important."

The current picture is a difficult one for gay and trans people in football at all levels.

The grassroots game is where the bulk of the increase in abuse has occurred, says Kick It Out, which claims it received 140% more reports last year than in the 2024-25 season. Three quarters of these reports are from senior grassroots games, where the players are over 18.

Away from football, research by Stonewall published in October found 11% of LGBTQ+ people in the UK avoid the gym, exercise classes or sports groups for fear of discrimination. Among trans people, the figure rises to 29%.

It said 15% of LGBTQ+ people who had been to a live sporting event, or watched sport in a bar, in the past year had experienced discrimination there. This rose to 26% for trans people.

"What we know is that there is a lot of work going on around equality and diversity; we also know homophobia and transphobia continue to be rife," Blake said.

"We are in a world, whether at Premier League or grassroots football, where views that may have been perceived to be unacceptable are now being expressed freely. That influences peoples' relationship with sport."

Premier League With Pride will return in 2026-27.

"The matchday activations take place in February in line with LGBTQ+ History Month, when the league and clubs will showcase their commitment to LGBTQ+ inclusion," a Premier League spokesperson told BBC Sport.

"There will be two match rounds dedicated to Premier League With Pride. This means all 20 clubs have a home game during that period, providing an opportunity to highlight and celebrate the LGBTQ+ community in football and showcase the work undertaken to make the game more inclusive.

"There is no centralised activation lined up for November."

#826. What's at the top of Frick's Aberdeen to-do list?

Swiss club Luzern did not renew Mario Frick's contract this summer

Mario Frick arrives at Aberdeen with the Pittodrie side sitting second bottom of the table and a game against relegation rivals Kilmarnock first up.

Lose that match and they fall to the foot of the Scottish Premiership. No pressure.

Apart from the obvious, what is it that the new head coach has to do to restore Aberdeen to previous glory days and avoid becoming yet another managerial failure at Pittodrie?

Okay, maybe this was obvious. But it's Aberdeen's clearest weakness this season.

They have the joint worst attacking record in the league, having only scored 12 goals and routinely looked completely short of confidence in front of goal.

Kevin Nisbet, the club captain, has 14 goals for the season. Nine of those came in the run to the Premier Sports Cup semi-final. Behind him, no-one has more than two.

Most concerning of all is that the Dons' have created the lowest xG (15.3) in the league so far. Not only are they not creating very many quality chances, they're struggling to take them.

They have just 3.3 shots on target per match, with a shot conversion rate of just 7.3%. Both metrics are the worst in the league.

Only Falkirk have created fewer big chances (19 to Aberdeen's 22) - the difference being John McGlynn's side score them.

Getting the best out of Connor Ronan could be key for Mario Frick

One of the most frequent accusations that came predecessor Stephen Robinson's way was that his team lacked an identity and players looked unsure as to the tactical plan they had been told to carry out.

Given the Northern Irishman's clear style of play with St Mirren, that was a surprise.

His team in Paisley were known for their physically-domineering displays that were full of grit and graft. That wasn't the case in the North East.

Frick seemingly prefers a 4-4-2 formation, with the midfield playing in a diamond.

That might be bad news for new signings Tony Yogane and Lewis Smith, wingers who did get a look in under Robinson but struggled to make much of an impact.

Sticking to a consistent midfield will help with that. While Robinson regularly relied on Afeez Aremu in the middle of the park, the head coach often chopped and changed his midfield partner.

Of all of Aberdeen's 15 summer signings, Connor Ronan was the one that probably caused the most optimism. Another former St Mirren man, he impressed in his time in Paisley.

The Irishman won a move to Major League Soccer with Colorado Rapids off the back of that form and was also called up to the Republic of Ireland squad without winning a cap.

Eight goals from midfield in the 2021-22 season was a good return - and a couple of them were screamers.

Former Aberdeen midfielder Jamie McGrath recently reminded his old fanbase that they could do with replacing him after he scored a rocket for Hibs in the 4-0 win that did for Robinson.

Ronan could be the answer, playing in a similar role with the same attacking capabilities.

He has yet to hit the heights at Pittodrie, but if Frick can make him tick, the 28-year-old could fire Aberdeen back up the league table.

#824. Vinicius says transfer interest affected Real form

Vinicius Jr signed a new six-year contract with Real Madrid in August

Real Madrid forward Vinicius Jr says he felt "truly overwhelmed" by transfer speculation in the summer, which has contributed to his mixed form at the start of the season.

The Brazil international has scored just once and provided three assists in 12 appearances for Jose Mourinho's side this season.

He was linked with a move to Premier League champions Arsenal this summer as he entered the final year of his contract, before signing an extension at Real.

The 26-year-old also says he did not train as much as he should have following Brazil's last-16 exit at the World Cup.

"I don't think I prepared as well as I could have after the World Cup, because the impact of that tournament is so significant for all Brazilians," he said.

"Being knocked out so early was something we hadn't expected. So, I took advantage of my holidays to enjoy myself, rest, relax, and spend more time with my family. I ended up training less than in previous years.

"That may have affected my start to the season.

"On top of that, regarding my contract renewal, with so many clubs showing interest last summer, I felt truly overwhelmed, as with the situation at Real Madrid. But it's a very long season."

Vinicius received a red card for violent conduct in October when he pulled the hair of Villarreal midfielder Nathan Saliba, which led to a four-match suspension.

In his absence, record signing Yan Diomande has made the most of his opportunity on the left wing, scoring four goals.

Vinicius joined Real from Brazilian side Flamengo in 2018 and has scored more than 20 club goals in each of his past five seasons.

Mourinho's side are second in La Liga, three points behind rivals Barcelona, and return to league action when they host Celta Vigo on Saturday.

#822. Melissa Gorga to Debut ‘Sunday Sauce’ Video Podcast This December (Exclusive)

The launch of the new podcast arrives just in time for the return of 'The Real Housewives of New Jersey.'

Melissa Gorga isn’t only returning to reality television this December; she’s also returning to the podcasting space.

The Real Housewives of New Jersey star is set to debut her new Sunday Sauce podcast on Sunday, Dec. 6, on the fwd. Network. The weekly video podcast will feature a rotating panel of celebrity guests every other week; her husband, Joe Gorga, will join her in episodes on the alternating weeks.

“Every family’s got one night a week where the truth comes out. In my family, it’s always Sunday,” Gorga says in the trailer for the new show. “When you join me on Sundays, nobody’s safe. Not my family, not my friends, not who’s ever brave enough to sit down in front of me!” Related Stories Business Former NBA Star Jalen Rose Launching Sports and Culture Talk Show "Pop The Trunk" (Exclusive) Business How 'The Basement Yard' Host Joe Santagato Got Into the World of 'Hot Ones'

Some of her first guests include Hilaria Baldwin, Dolores Catania, Harry Jowsey, Nicole “Snooki” Polizzi and the upcoming new season 15 cast of the New Jersey-based Real Housewives.

“Growing up in an Italian family, Sunday sauce meant everyone around the table, talking, laughing and holding nothing back. That’s exactly what this podcast is,” Gorga said in a statement. “Fans have watched my life on TV for more than 15 years. This is a chance to have the conversations that don’t make it to air. They’re honest, they’re funny, and they’re a little bit saucy.”

Gorga previously hosted the On Display with Melissa Gorga podcast, which ran weekly from December 2021 to July 2025. Her new podcast announcement trails the long-awaited return of RHONJ on Bravo this December.

Sunday Sauce will feature segments such as “Big Glass, ‘Tini Questions,” where Gorga will answer fan questions out of an oversized martini glass, and “Cheers and Booze,” a rapid-fire round of one win to celebrate and one gripe to let out.

The podcast name “Sunday Sauce” is a callback also to Gorga’s recipe of the same name that she’s shared online.

“Melissa has built a remarkable career on her own terms, from television to the businesses she’s created, and women see themselves in her story,” said Cathy Csukas, CEO of AdLarge and the fwd. Network. “fwd. was created so women like Melissa have a place where their voices are heard, and Sunday Sauce is exactly that: honest, funny and unapologetically her. We’re thrilled to welcome her to the network.”

Gorga returns to RHONJ alongside former Housewives Teresa Giudice and Catania, alongside a fully rebooted cast. The series has been on pause, with the most recent episode, the season 14 finale, airing over two years ago in August 2024.

Tune into @SundaySauceShow on YouTube, plus Gorga’s socials, for episode updates and behind-the-scenes moments.

#821. This AI ‘mechanic’ can peer inside the black box of other neural networks

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Some AI models behave like mechanics — fixing issues in other models that they neither designed nor fully understand. Credit: Mint Images/Getty

Researchers have used an artificial-intelligence model to read and tinker with the internal workings of another AI network — offering a new way to peek into the ‘black box’ of AI.

Computer scientists usually improve models by training them in tiny increments or by building them from scratch. A team at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) in Cambridge has demonstrated how an AI model called GPT-6 Astra can interpret the raw internal values of some other models well enough to predict what different parts of the systems do. It can then edit the models to make improvements — including boosting their mathematical abilities. The authors reported their findings in a preprint1 on 2 November.

ChatGPT is a black box: how AI research can break it open

ChatGPT is a black box: how AI research can break it open

Frontier AI models are “showing early sparks” of an ability to treat neural networks like files that they can read, reason about and change, says co-author Rikiya Takehi, a machine-learning researcher at MIT.

The results do not mean that Astra, developed by OpenAI in San Francisco, California, can explain or understand how a given AI network works. But the findings suggest that general-purpose AI models — such as ChatGPT or Claude — might be able to modify a network in useful ways, like a mechanic who can identify and fix issues in an engine that they neither designed nor fully understand.

Researchers already try to interpret how different components of a network create its outputs. The preprint shows that it is possible to automate some of these ‘interpretability’ methods, says Fazl Barez, an AI-safety researcher at the University of Oxford, UK.

Researchers hope that better understanding models in this way will help to create safer AI systems, although Barez cautions that this assumption is “largely untested”.

It remains unclear if Astra is going beyond applying information and techniques learned in its training. Barez says he would be surprised if Astra is able to read and interpret models in ways that go beyond existing human abilities.

Three reasons why AI is not conscious and perhaps never will be

Three reasons why AI is not conscious and perhaps never will be

Still, if developed further, such ability to reprogram models might be an asset in developing AI for science, says Marinka Zitnik, a computer scientist and bioinformatician at Harvard University in Cambridge, Massachusetts. For example, it could help to spot errors in a model ahead of real-world testing, she says.

Frontier AI systems are based on massive neural networks — brain-inspired architectures in which layers of processing units, or neurons, are linked by billions of ‘weights’, values that represent the strength of connections inside a model. The strength of each weight is slowly nudged during training to make the model better at, for example, predicting a protein structure or the next word in a sentence.

The complex way in which a model’s features link to its outputs means they are often described as black boxes. Interpretability researchers run experiments to work out, for example, which weights are activated under specific conditions. Researchers have also previously developed custom models that can learn to edit other models2.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03679-8

Takehi, R., Teoh, J., Zhang, A. & Khattab, O. Preprint at alphaXiv https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2611.weight-space-programming (2026).

Schmidhuber, J. Neural Comput. 4, 131–139 (1992).

#819. Russell Brand’s Wife Breaks Silence on His Conviction, Prison Sentence

Russell Brand's wife Laura Brand shared her first public comments since her husband was sentenced to 10 years in prison after being convicted of rape and sexual assault.

Russell Brand’s wife Laura Brand is adjusting to a new reality.

Days after the British comedian was sentenced to over 10 years in prison following his rape and sexual assault conviction, his wife spoke out in her first comments since the news, sharing the fate of their weekly faith podcast Sunday Service with The Brands.

“I’m here to continue the good work that was being established here in this Sunday Service community,” Laura told the camera on the Nov. 15 episode. “Something very close to mine and Russell's hearts.”

“It may look different,” she continued, “but the ambitions are very much the same.”

The 39-year-old—who shares three kids with Russell—admitted that she’s turning to her faith as she moves forward with the show without her husband.

“We trust God, and we trust his plan, and we trust everything He’s doing right now, even though it’s painful,” Laura shared. “And obviously [it] will take some getting used to for me to even sit here and not have my companion and my person with me.”

After thanking fans for their “support,” the mom of three noted that she’s been speaking with Russell.

“He’s OK and he’s praying, unsurprisingly,” Laura told the camera. “He’s praying and we decided for me to continue.”

Laura’s video comes on the heels of Russell’s conviction and prison sentencing.

On Nov. 5, the 51-year-old—who had pleaded guilty to all charges—was convicted by a London court on one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault for events that allegedly occurred between 1999 and 2009.

Although Russell was convicted of four charges, he was cleared of two separate counts of rape and one count of indecent assault.

However, days later, on Nov. 9, judge Joel Bennathan sentenced Russell to 10 years and six months in prison, according to The Telegraph.

While the Forgetting Sarah Marshall actor’s sentencing concludes his case that began in April 2025, his legal battle may not have reached its end.

Following Russell’s Nov. 5 conviction, the Metropolitan Police of London confirmed to E! News an investigation into the former reality TV presenter is still ongoing after two additional allegations of rape were brought forward.

“The suspect has previously been interviewed under caution in connection with the allegations,” the statement noted. “Files have been submitted to the Crown Prosecution Service in relation to both complainants. Detectives remain in close contact with prosecutors as enquiries continue and further investigative work is carried out.”

For a detailed look back at Brand’s trial, keep reading…

Russell Brand was charged with rape and sexual assault in April 2025.

The London Metropolitan Police charged Brand for one count of rape, two counts of indecent assault and one count of indecent assault in April 2025 for events that transpired between 1999 and 2005.

At the time, Brand immediately denied the allegations in a video response, noting he was receiving “egregious attacks” from the media in addition to the allegations.

“Amidst this litany of astonishing, rather baroque attacks are some very serious allegations,” Brand said in a video shared to social media at the time, “that I absolutely refute.”

Russell Brand pleaded not guilty to all charges.

Though the Forgetting Sarah Marshall star had previously written in a 2007 essay for The Guardian that he had a “sexy addiction” and “disregard for social conventions of sexual protocol,” he vehemently denied the charges against him.

In his video statement, Brand admitted he had been a “fool” in the past, although maintained he never partook in “non-consensual activity.”

“I was a fool before I lived in the light of the Lord,” Brand said in a video shared to his X account in April 2025. “I was a drug addict, a sex addict and an imbecile, but what I never was, was a rapist.”

In the same video, Brand noted he was “grateful” to have the opportunity to fight the allegations in court.  He pleaded not guilty to all five charges in May 2025.

Russell Brand was served with two more sexual offense charges in December 2025.

In December 2025, the London Metropolitan Police charged Brand with one additional count of rape and one additional count of sexual assault regarding incidents that took place with two separate women in 2009.

Brand responded to the charges in a separate video posted to his social media.

“I pray Lord, anyone that I’ve harmed or hurt in my years of mindlessness and sin would be healed, Lord,” he said in the clip. “And I pray, Lord, for the absolute truth of who I am to be abundantly revealed.”

With the additional allegations, Brand was charged with three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one count of indecent assault involving six women for events that transpired between 1999 and 2009. He later pleaded not guilty to the additional charges.

Russell Brand was found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault.

In a November 2026 ruling, a London court found Brand guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. He was cleared of two additional counts of rape and one count of indecent assault.

During the trial, Brand maintained his innocence and said that while he dedicated much of his life to “beyond reckless philandering,” per the New York Times, he never engaged in non-consensual activities.

Russell Brand was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison.

After confirming he would sentence the Get Him to the Greek alum with “significant custodial time,” during the ruling and denying him bail, presiding judge Joel Bennathan sentenced Brand to 10 years and six months in prison.

During the Nov. 9, 2026 sentencing, Bennathan called Brand a “sexual predator,” and commended the women who testified for their “determination and bravery.”

Bennathan said he considered Brand’s family in his ruling, calling his decision a “sad loss” for Brand’s three children, whom he shares with wife Laura Brand.

However, the judge noted that Brand had brought the decision “upon himself,” noting the comedian had acted with “casual, arrogant disregard,” for women.

Russell Brand legal team said he is a “fundamentally different person” now.

Prior to the sentencing, Brand’s lawyer Ian Winter KC said his client is “fundamentally a different person today,” than he was when the incidents took place, per CBS News.

Winter noted that the rape for which Brand was found guilty—which took place in 2009—was a “momentary total failure.”

Brand is also represented by Oliver Schneider-Sikorsky. His legal team will have the opportunity to appeal.

#818. Who swaggered around like he owned the place? Spain v England ratings

Ben White scored England's third goal on his first start for the team since March 2022

England went 3-0 up before surviving a late onslaught after going down to 10 men to earn a landmark victory against World Cup holders Spain in Madrid on Sunday night.

Here's how we rated the players following the Three Lions' 3-2 victory and you can see how you scored them below.

Unai Simon: Made some brilliant saves early in the first half but still conceded three. 7

Marc Pubill: Had a bright 20 minutes against Anthony Gordon until he came off injured. 6

Pau Cubarsi: Gave away the penalty that Harry Kane scored for England's opener. 5

Aymeric Laporte: Always under pressure against Kane but came into the game more as the England striker dropped deeper after the sending off. 7

Marc Cucarella: Tried to get under Morgan Rogers' skin and kept him fairly quiet. 6

Martin Zubimendi: Made some decent challenges. 6

Fabian Ruiz: Made little impact in midfield before he came off at half-time. 5

Mikel Merino: The Arsenal midfielder was ineffective and quiet for the first half - and then taken off at half-time. 5

Lamine Yamal: Lewis Hall and Jarell Quansah has to double up to contain him. Moments of brilliance throughout. 8

Alex Baena: The Atletico Madrid forward made some decent runs into the box. 7

Mikel Oyarzabal: Scored Spain's penalty to make it 3-1. Relatively quiet other than that. 7

Pedro Porro (on 20, Pubill): Worked hard against Gordon. Had a great chance against James Trafford. 7

Jarell Quansah: Was having a good night until making the mistake that led to Spain's opener from the spot and Anderson's red card. 5

Lewis Hall: Growing in stature at international level. Excelled in the attacking third and battled well against Yamal. 8

Elliot Anderson: Utterly brilliant until being shown a red card in trying to clear up Quansah's mess. Desperately unlucky. 8

Declan Rice: Organised and drove the team forward - all while on an early yellow card. Delivered the corner for England's second. 8

Jude Bellingham: In his adopted city, the Real Madrid midfielder swaggered around like he owned the place. Oozed quality. 9

Morgan Rogers: A disciplined display from the Chelsea forward and still created Spain problems in forward areas. 8

Anthony Gordon: A nuisance for Spain in every area of the field but dalliance in possession led to host's second to set up anxious finish. 6

Harry Kane: Won and dispatched England's penalty and Spain could not live with his intelligence at times. Sacrificed following Anderson's red card. 7

Subs not used: Pickford, Steele, Hill, Alexander-Arnold, Gibbs-White, Jobe Bellingham, Eze, Ngumoha.

#817. Harry Styles Shut Out of the 2027 Grammy Nominations

The British singer has previously won three Grammys and recently wrapped up his 30-show residency at New York's Madison Square Garden.

Harry Styles has been shut out of the 2027 Grammy nominations.

Styles’ fourth studio album, Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally, was released March 6 and features 12 songs. The album debuted at No. 1 on the U.S. Billboard 200, while its lead single, “Aperture,” reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100.

The former One Direction member has previously won three Grammys. He earned his first in 2021 for best pop solo performance for “Watermelon Sugar” before taking home album of the year and best pop vocal album honors for Harry’s House at the 65th Grammy Awards in 2023. Related Stories Music 2027 Grammy Nominations: Raye, Rosalía Lead a Women-Dominated General Field Music Grammy Nominations: Watch the Livestream

The 2027 Grammy nominations come just two weeks after Styles completed his historic 30-show residency at Madison Square Garden as part of his Together, Together tour. The singer wrapped up the run on Halloween, with the final performance also serving as the second night of his Harryween celebrations.

The Hollywood Reporter was in attendance for both the opening night of the residency, where Styles performed a tribute to the late Dolly Parton, and the final show. During the Halloween performance, Styles appeared in a rodent costume and was joined by New York Knicks star Jalen Brunson, who presented him with a banner celebrating his record-breaking 30-show run.

Styles is next set to resume his Together, Together tour in Melbourne, Australia, on Nov. 27 before wrapping up the 2026 run in Sydney in December. He will return to North America in April 2027, kicking off the next leg in Phoenix before continuing across the U.S. and Canada. The tour will then head to Europe, concluding with three shows at London’s Wembley Stadium on Aug. 25, 27 and 28.

The 69th Annual Grammy Awards will take place Feb. 7 at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles with the music awards show airing live on ABC.

Raye leads this year’s Grammy nominations with 11 nods, followed by Rosalía with nine and Ella Langley, Olivia Rodrigo, Phoebe Bridgers and Miranda Lambert with seven nods apiece.

#816. Is Scotland's system limiting Gannon-Doak's threat?

Is Scotland's system limiting Ben Gannon-Doak's threat?

Two years ago, when Scotland defeated Croatia in the Nations League, that November night at Hampden was the dawn of Ben Gannon-Doak.

The then-teenager took Â£77m Manchester City man Josko Gvardiol to the cleaners and fans demanded the national team be built around the winger.

The Tartan Army's love for him has never faded - it arguably peaked when he stole the show in Scotland's World Cup opening win over Haiti - but it is fair to say they are growing frustrated, arguably on the Bournemouth man's behalf.

Under Sebastien Pocognoli, Gannon-Doak - who turned 21 on Wednesday - has been deployed at right wing-back, a role that demands defensive instincts unnatural to the pacy attacker.

It is already clear the new head coach is wedded to his preferred system, but it is one that is stifling one of Scotland's greatest attacking outlets - even though his final product still leaves a lot to be desired.

As his side prepare to visit Nations League Group B1 leaders Switzerland on Monday needing a win to have any chance of a promotion play-off place, Pocognoli has addressed both concerns - citing he is not uneasy about either - but pundits and punters alike cannot seem to shift their suspicions.

In that 1-0 victory over 10-man Croatia, it was Gannon-Doak's fearlessness in facing one of Europe's most elite and experienced teams that caught the eye.

His electric speed and directness excited a support who had long been crying out for a player with such qualities and the confidence in applying them. A natural winger, if you will.

In Pocognoli's system, though, there is no space for wingers. Something that former Rangers full-back Richard Foster says must "scunner" the wee man.

"When you're a full-back and you get to play wing-back, it's amazing - all of a sudden you are 10-20 yards up the pitch, doing more attacking and you can be a bit more aggressive," he said on BBC Scotland's Sportsound.

"When you ask a winger to do that, most of the time they are absolutely scunnered. They are thinking 'I don't want to go back there'.

Why 'inspiring' Van Gaal influences Scotland head coach Pocognoli

Six goals to go - will McGinn catch Dalglish & Law?

"Looking at the squad [against North Macedonia], the three most exciting players we had - Findlay Curtis, Josh McPake and Gannon-Doak - are all wingers and he didn't bring two on.

"You look at the previous game [against Slovenia] and the difference McPake and Curtis made by coming on and taking players on - it gives everyone a lift.

"As a fan, you want to get excited about what you are watching. We are playing in a shape where we have the most exciting talents on the bench and they can't get on unless you adjust things. I just think he has to change the formation."

Foster is far from the only one wishing for a shift in shape - and not just for Gannon-Doak's benefit. Much has been made about the Scots' options in defence, too, and whether they match-up to the method.

However, it is arguable Gannon-Doak is the biggest casualty of them all.

"I don't think we're getting the best out of Ben," former Scotland captain Scott Brown told BBC Scotland.

"You saw him making so many last-ditch headers on Friday. He's having to add things to his game that he probably hasn't done before, like throw-ins, defending one-v-one."

No need to mention that throw-in, Scott. But that wasn't the only instance where Gannon-Doak looked a little lost. Think the 'Confused Travolta' meme.

While his position is a new worry, his precision with his final product is not.

Almost in a microcosm, Gannon-Doak's play was laid bare when be hurtled to the byeline before winning what turned out to be the match-winning penalty against the North Macedonians on Friday.

"He made a great run for the penalty, but I did think he could have got his shot away a bit earlier and maybe not taken that extra touch," Brown said.

Back in 2024, the wee live-wire was forgiven for not always finding a pal with a pass or choking at crunch time with his final ball.

However, as the years go on and the caps rack up, his shortcomings are still on show. His end product is still largely poor and patience is wearing thin.

"As long as he is high on the pitch and is creating one-v-ones, I am happy," Pocognoli reiterated post his maiden Hampden win.

"With Ben, we know that he is a young age and needs to work on specific things. On Friday night, he had great opportunities.

"We know that he needs to improve on the end product. But he created a penalty and, against Slovenia and North Macedonia away, he created a number of unbelievable one-v-ones. He did that on Friday night as well.

"We know he can be good if we dominate the game and he can get in good positions if we control the ball.

So Pocognoli is comfortable for now. Already that appears to be a running theme for the head coach - even if others are not.

#815. How did England cling on against Spain and what did Tuchel do differently?

James Trafford (right) kept Spain out in the latter stages

England held on to beat Spain 3-2 with a backs-to-the-wall finale in the Nations League to finish top of their group.

But many observers would have been feeling a sense of deja vu from the World Cup semi-final when England sat back and were beaten by Argentina.

So what was different this time? BBC Sport has a look.

First of all the context of the two games was entirely different.

England were 1-0 up against Argentina in the 55th minute on neutral territory in Atlanta - and still had all their players.

Anthony Gordon had put them ahead but Lionel Messi set up Enzo Fernandez and then Lautaro Martinez late on.

But against Spain the best performance of Thomas Tuchel's reign had them 3-0 up through goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White.

Elliot Anderson then fouled Lamine Yamal for a penalty, which Mikel Oyarzabal scored - and that began the siege at a partisan Riyadh Air Metropolitano.

Nico Williams made it 3-2 but Spain could not find an equaliser, thanks in part to England keeper James Trafford.

"Half an hour feels like two hours against a team like this [with 10 men]," Tuchel told ITV afterwards. "That's the way it is. Without the red card we were clear winners."

60 minutes of perfection, 30 minutes of chaos - an England win for the ages

England cling on to stun world champions Spain in thriller

Making defensive subs is fine when it works - but when it does not, boy will a manager hear about it.

In the World Cup last 16, England had been 2-1 up against Mexico in the Azteca when Jarell Quansah was sent off.

Tuchel brought on three defenders for a defender, a midfielder and a forward.

But England won 3-2 and Dan Burn's cameo was the stuff of legend.

However, nine days later with England 1-0 up against Argentina, Tuchel did the same again - three defenders on for a defender, midfielder and forward.

The first of those subs, with Konsa replacing Anthony Gordon, was in the 72nd minute.

And England just sat back until Argentina broke their resistance.

However, against Spain this time, despite England being down to 10 men and facing incessant pressure, Tuchel was not so quick with defensive subs.

Myles Lewis-Skelly, replacing Harry Kane, was the first on after 78 minutes - 15 minutes after Anderson's sending off. And then five minutes later he brought on two more players - but one of them was a striker in Dominic Calvert-Lewin.

Burn replaced fellow defender White in the 89th minute.

"Harry played 78 minutes, Jude [Bellingham] 83 minutes and then just defending and defending, it's tiring," explained Tuchel.

"So we needed fresh energy. I was asked yesterday what happens if there needs to be a critical or crucial substitution. And I said, I feel free enough to take any substitution if I think it is necessary to help the team and to influence the game.

"I feel free enough to do that and I think there was a lot of defending needed. So we just went for some fresh legs."

Win over world champions Spain is a 'statement' - Tuchel

England actually faced more of a siege this time than against the Argentines, the stats confirm.

In the final 30 minutes they faced 19 shots from Spain, with seven on target and an expected goals (xG) total of 2.53.

Argentina, in that time, had 10 shots, with four on target and an xG of 1.41.

In terms of passes from England the numbers were similar with 65 against Argentina and 61 against Spain - both times with an accuracy rate of about 64%.

In Thursday's 2-1 win against Croatia, as a comparison, they tried 557 passes with accuracy of 89%.

"For half an hour it was Mexico reloaded and it felt like we were back in the Azteca. We had to overcome 30 minutes which, against Spain, felt like three hours," Tuchel told BBC Radio 5 Live.

"The difficult thing is it's not only a red card, it's a red card, and a goal so that makes a completely new game. Thirty minutes against the world champion feels like three hours. I said it before in the stadium and wave after wave after wave."

England were criticised for blowing a 2-1 half-time lead at Wembley in their first Nations League game with Spain.

But on that day their final 30-minute figurers were much better - with only five shots faced and 176 attempted passes with a 90% accuracy.

So what was different this time? Perhaps the team showed more resilience and unity?

After Spain had pulled one back England's players had a huddle.

"I love the fact the team went into a huddle and if anything the manager's stepped back because he wants to see the player reaction," said ex-England defender Matt Upson on BBC Radio 5 Live.

"I almost think that the trauma from that sending off of Elliot Anderson has almost been a positive thing for England because it's given the team a chance to get together and cope in what is an incredibly difficult situation and come through the other side.

"There was so much going on in this game. England had to suffer and came through the other side."

Defender and goalscorer White was asked about the huddle after the game.

"Just stay calm, when you're one down it becomes more difficult and things change so it was all about managing that," he said.

Another factor was the performance of England keeper James Trafford, who made six saves - with four of them coming in the final 12 minutes of the game with the score at 3-2.

He made an incredible double save to deny Fermin Lopez and Lamine Yamal in injury time.

Upson said: "I think that double save was the moment for Spain and Trafford had the answers."

#814. Ariana Grande Lands Four Grammy Nominations, Including Song of the Year Nod, After “Taking a Step Back From Visibility”

The nominations come months after the 'Wicked' star released her eighth studio album, 'Petal,' and wrapped up her Eternal Sunshine Tour.

Ariana Grande has received four nominations for the 2027 Grammys.

Grande’s nominations, which were announced Monday morning, include a song of the year nod for “Hate That I Made You Love Me,” which also scored a best music video nod, as well as noms for best pop vocal album (Petal) and best traditional pop vocal performance for her “For Good” duet from Wicked: For Good alongside Cynthia Erivo.

In the song of the year category, Grande is nominated alongside Rosalía’s “Berghain,” Ella Langley’s “Choosin’ Texas,” Olivia Rodrigo’s “The Cure,” Taylor Swift’s “I Knew It, I Knew You,” Olivia Dean’s “Man I Need,” Bruno Mars’ “Risk It All” and Raye’s “Where Is My Husband!” Related Stories Music 2027 Grammy Nominations: Raye, Rosalía Lead a Women-Dominated General Field Music Grammy Nominations: Watch the Livestream

Most of Grande’s nominations come in support of her eighth studio album, Petal, released July 31. The 12-track album debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200.

The singer has previously won three Grammys. She earned her first in 2019 for best pop vocal album for Sweetener, followed by best pop duo/group performance for “Rain on Me” with Lady Gaga in 2021 and, earlier this year, for her and Erivo’s “Defying Gravity” from the first Wicked film.

The 2027 Grammy nominations come more than two months after Grande wrapped up her Eternal Sunshine Tour, with her final performance taking place in London on Sept. 1. Her 2024 album, Eternal Sunshine, earned three Grammy nominations but was shut out at the 67th Annual Grammy Awards.

In recent years, Grande has also returned to acting, starring as Glinda the Good Witch in Jon M. Chu’s Wicked (2024) and Wicked: For Good (2025). The role earned her an Oscar nomination for best supporting actress at the 97th Academy Awards.

In August, Grande’s representative shared a statement with The Hollywood Reporter saying that the singer would be “taking a step back from visibility” after finishing her Eternal Sunshine Tour. The statement came amid “ongoing public scrutiny” and a wave of online commentary surrounding her health and body. Grande also dropped out of the West End revival of Stephen Sondheim’s Sunday in the Park With George, which was set to feature her Wicked co-star Jonathan Bailey.

Last week, Grande attended the premiere of Focker-in-Law, where she posed for photos with her boyfriend, Ricky Alvarez. The film, which also stars Robert De Niro, Ben Stiller and Styler Gisondo, is set to hit theaters Nov. 25. Grande will then lend her voice to the upcoming animated adaptation of the Dr. Seuss book Oh, the Places You’ll Go!, from directors Jon M. Chu and Jill Culton, which is set to arrive in theaters March 17, 2028.

The 69th Annual Grammy Awards will take place Feb. 7 at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, with the music awards show airing live on ABC.

Raye leads this year’s Grammy nominations with 11 nods, followed by Rosalía with nine and Ella Langley, Olivia Rodrigo, Phoebe Bridgers and Miranda Lambert with seven nods apiece.

#813. Pregnant Brittany Mahomes Attends Chiefs Game After Sharing Baby News

Brittany Mahomes made her first appearance since revealing she's pregnant with her and Patrick Mahomes' fourth baby by supporting her husband at the Kansas City Chiefs game Nov. 15,

Brittany Mahomes is entering her pregnancy season once again.

Five days after the wife of Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes revealed she’s expecting the couple’s fourth child, she made her first public appearance since sharing the exciting news, stepping out to cheer on her husband in his NFL game against the Atlanta Falcons in Atlanta Nov. 15.

For the occasion, Brittany—who shares kids Sterling, 5, Bronze, 3, and Golden, 21 months, with Patrick—wore a Chiefs red jacket and oversized black sunglasses, styling her blond locks in a wavy ponytail.

And, of course, the 31-year-old brought her winning team to support Patrick on the field.

After all, Brittany shared fun videos of her kids enjoying some family fun before the Chiefs and the Falcons faced off.

In an adorable clip posted to her Instagram Stories Nov. 15, the Kansas City Current co-owner carried Golden through the stadium tunnel out onto the field, noting her daughter didn’t arrive empty-handed.

“This child literally walked into the stadium with [a] waffle in hand,” Brittany shared as her youngest ate her snack. “No waffle left behind!”

And just like her mom, the toddler arrived at the game in style, wearing a white jacket that featured her dad’s name and jersey number in red on her back, along with matching red ruffled leggings.

Golden matched with her older sister Sterling, who also sported Chiefs red leggings under a pink dress.

And as the Mahomes crew huddled up to watch Patrick score another win for the Chiefs, they are continuing to celebrate the exciting news of adding another player to their team.

On Nov. 10, Brittany and Patrick announced they’re expecting their fourth baby together.

“Another blessing from God,” the couple wrote in a joint Instagram post alongside sweet family photos, including a shot of their kids with their hands on Brittany’s baby bump. “& then there were 6.”

Though the pair—who tied the knot in 2022—haven’t shared whether they’re expecting a boy or girl, Patrick joked that he has one play he may prefer.

As the 31-year-old told reporters during a Nov. 11 press conference, “I’m hoping that me and Bronze can even up the score.”

But Patrick emphasized that all that matters is that his and Brittany’s new arrival is “healthy.”

“Obviously, it’s a blessing to have another baby on the way,” he shared. “I’m excited for it.”

#812. 60 minutes of perfection, 30 minutes of chaos - an England win for the ages

Harry Kane scored for a record-equalling seventh England away game

Thomas Tuchel went with bold words when reminded about the caution that sabotaged England's World Cup hopes and left them with so much to prove against Spain in the Nations League on Sunday.

In a media theatre at the Metropolitano in Madrid, head coach Tuchel's sixth sense led him to go public with what he was convinced England would produce against the world champions.

Tuchel looked his inquisitors in the eyes and declared: "We are up for something spectacular."

To say Tuchel and England kept their word was a masterpiece of understatement after the finest night of the head coach's reign resulted in a 3-2 victory that was large parts magnificent, some parts madness - and all parts spectacular.

It also ended Spain's 43-game unbeaten run - setting aside their penalty shootout defeat by Portugal in the 2025 Nations League final.

If England and Tuchel could be accused of being cowed by pressure when they led Argentina in the ill-fated World Cup semi-final, they were thrillingly positive in this unforgiving Madrid environment.

The question being asked when England held a one-goal advantage through Harry Kane's penalty at half-time was 'what would theirs and Tuchel's reaction be?' Stick or twist?

Would Tuchel tell England to press their foot on the pedal for acceleration? Or would he take the approach of going into reverse gear, as he did to ill-fated effect against Argentina?

How did England cling on against Spain and what did Tuchel do differently?

Who swaggered around like he owned the place? Spain v England ratings

England hold on to stun world champions Spain in thriller

The answer was delivered when they added goals from Arsenal duo Ezri Konsa and Ben White in the first 12 minutes of the second half.

This being England, they then created a mess for themselves when Elliot Anderson was sent off for fouling Lamine Yamal in the area after 65 minutes, although the main culprit was Jarell Quansah for initially conceding possession.

Mikel Oyarzabal scored from the spot and, when Yamal set up Nico Williams for Spain's second with 15 minutes left, it looked like more than an hour of faultless England football might be wasted.

But not a bit of it, as goalkeeper James Trafford produced heroics and England defended with every fibre to close out this landmark win.

Was this the statement victory that was almost demanded of Tuchel as recompense for the World Cup disappointment, a performance to convince the doubters?

"We're fully aware what we put out there," said Tuchel afterwards. "What a performance we put out for 65 minutes to be deservedly 3-0 up.

"Of course, the red card and the penalty changed the momentum and the characteristics of the game... but we know, and the players know very, very well, what they put out there. That is the statement - and that is the significance of this victory."

Simple details of the game barely touch the sides of a night filled with quality and glorious chaos, vindication for Tuchel and England's positive approach.

Spain opened with an ostentatious parade of the World Cup in front of England's players as the teams lined up, perhaps a psychological reminder of the superiority that has seen them dominate international football.

What followed, at times literally, reduced Spain's supporters to stunned silence and their players to a shell-shocked shambles chasing the shadows that were overpowering them.

England's white shirts were everywhere but Spain could not get near them. The tormentors had become the tormented.

It was alien territory for a Spain side that has carried all before them, while England's fans tucked away high in a corner of this vast arena were equally unbelieving as a dream unfolded in front of them.

England, for 65 minutes, were in a different class to Spain. And, yes, you have read that right.

From the first whistle, employing a suffocatingly high press, England ran all over Spain.

When White crowned a superb move with the third goal four minutes after Konsa's second, it looked, remarkably, to be a case of how big England's victory margin would be.

In the end, the margin was narrow but the stature and significance of England's victory was huge.

Tuchel labelled this meeting with Spain as "proof of concept at the highest level".

There was no doubt the German manager and England were under fierce scrutiny after the manner of the collapse, mentally and tactically, against Argentina at the World Cup.

Here they delivered the proof they can match the best then beat them.

Win over world champions Spain is a 'statement' - Tuchel

If the vital signs were being forensically examined for evidence Tuchel has learned lessons from a chastening World Cup, that England have improved after that harrowing experience, this game delivered these conclusions.

Of course, England must do it again. Do it when the pressure and expectation in at its highest.

The Nations League is competitive but cannot be compared to a World Cup and European Championship, both titles currently in the possession of the team they beat here.

But England's world-class players delivered - Kane inevitably with his 93rd international goal, but Jude Bellingham was on a level of his own, the outstanding performer on both sides with an individual display simply confirming he is the player with everything.

And Tuchel got his big calls right, especially selecting Trafford, who responded superbly in a frantic closing phase. White, making a strong claim for the right-back berth, not only scored a goal but produced crucial challenges in the face of relentless, albeit belated, Spain pressure.

"This was the highest level in terms of belief, team spirit, togetherness," said Tuchel. "It was on the highest level football wise in all aspects of the game. We did everything that needs to be done together.

"The deep build-up. The high press. The counter-attack. The tracking. The defensive phases. This was an excellent performance and of course a wonderful feeling for us in the dressing room.

"We overcame some difficult moments in the end. That's how it is. But we are very well aware which steps we took now through after the World Cup."

England's win means they top their Nations League group, but the importance spreads much wider than simply a league table.

The first 65 minutes were simply breathtaking. Spain wilting under attack after attack. Spain rattled until they shook as England refused to allow them meaningful possession.

After Anderson's dismissal, bad memories were revisited as England were forced into a rearguard action, but any other result than the one that was eventually delivered would have been a huge injustice.

England survived 29 nervous minutes, including added time, to make a powerful statement about their current status, which is much healthier than when recriminations about Tuchel's approach provided the post-World Cup narrative.

"I'm very impressed with the steps that we took after the World Cup", said Tuchel. "We wanted to get better, better in a deep build-up, get better in defending in a low block and, on top of it, we wanted always to impose our identity and the way we want to play against every opponent.

"I think this was clearly visible throughout the whole group phase. The results followed with an excellent group phase."

Was this the finest performance of Tuchel's time in charge? Most observers felt so, but the head coach was best placed to answer.

"Yes, given the circumstances," he said, "and the pressure, the quality, where we played in this building against the reigning world champions, unbeaten in 43 matches. Putting a performance out there in Madrid, and in this environment, was a very complete performance."

Tuchel will, of course, need repeat performances - but the outstanding ability and character England displayed here to beat the World Cup holders will deliver a huge injection of confidence and self-belief.

#810. 2027 Grammys: Madonna Lands Four Nods, Misses Out on Major Categories

The pop superstar makes a long-awaited return to music's biggest night by nabbing four nods for 'Confessions II,' her 16-song follow up to the 2005 chart-topping original, ‘Confessions.’

Madonna is nominated for the 2027 Grammys in the dance/electronic categories for Confessions II, but her latest album didn’t make it to the biggest categories.

The Grammy nods, the first for the pop superstar in 16 years, follow the release earlier this year of the 16-song Confessions II as a follow-up to the 2005 chart-topping original, Confessions on a Dance Floor. Madonna, who has seven Grammys under her belt, netted from Recording Academy voters nominations for best dance/electronic album for Confessions II, best dance/electronic recording for “I Feel So Free,” and best dance pop recording for “Danceteria.” Related Stories Music Ariana Grande Lands Four Grammy Nominations, Including Song of the Year Nod, After "Taking a Step Back From Visibility" Music Harry Styles Shut Out of the 2027 Grammy Nominations

Madonna also scored a Grammy nomination for best pop duo/group performance nomination along with Sabrina Carpenter for “Bring Your Love.” And her “Love Sensation” collaboration with Kylie Minogue landed a best remixed recording nod, but that nomination only goes to the remixer, Stuart Price.

Despite buzz going into the Grammy nominations reveal on Monday morning, Confessions II was shut out of the all-important record of the year, song of the year and album of the year categories. The four nominations do, however, end a drought for Madonna as her last Grammy award came in 2010 with “Celebration” winning for best dance recording. Her 28 Grammy nominations and seven trophies over the course of her career have come mostly in the dance song and electronic album categories, where Madonna had her biggest haul on Monday.

Confessions on a Dance Floor won best dance/electronic album at the Grammys in 2007. The 2027 Grammys will will take place Feb. 7 at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, with this year’s ceremony airing live at 7 p.m. ET / 4 p.m. PT on the Disney-owned ABC and streaming on Disney+ and Hulu.

#809. Republic of Ireland captain Collins to miss Kosovo game

Collins picked up a knee injury in the closing stages against Austria on Saturday

Republic of Ireland captain Nathan Collins has been ruled out of Tuesday's must-win Nations League game against Kosovo with a knee injury.

Defender Collins picked up the issue in the closing stages of Saturday's 1-0 defeat by Austria in Linz and has returned to his club Brentford for treatment.

Queens Park Rangers' Jimmy Dunne will replace Collins - who also missed all four games of the September/October window - in the matchday squad for the Kosovo fixture.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson has opted against drafting in Seamus Coleman, who is currently with the squad in a playing/coaching hybrid role.

"No, Jimmy Dunne will take Nathan's spot but we're really happy with what Seamus is giving to us," said Hallgrimsson.

"We obviously need to see the session today, that's the first session after the game, to see how players are but given everything I think we'll have the same squad including Jimmy."

Hallgrimsson rues 'painful' defeat for Republic of Ireland

The Republic of Ireland must win Tuesday's game to finish second in Group B3 and seal a place in March's promotion play-offs.

Hallgrimsson's side fell to a late 1-0 defeat by Kosovo in September before bouncing back to take four points from two matches against Israel.

"We need to get the same mentality, the same characters on the pitch against Kosovo," added Hallgrimsson.

"It is going to be as tough a game as it was in Austria, so just transfer that same attitude and if we do that, we will have a good byproduct, which is a win.

"It is clear we need to win the game, a draw will do nothing for us, and that is our mentality going into the game."

The Republic of Ireland's ultimate aim is securing a place at Euro 2028, which they will co-host alongside England, Wales and Scotland.

While goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher said playing in a tournament at home would be "amazing", he insisted the players are not looking that far ahead.

"Yeah, it would obviously be hard to describe, it would be an amazing experience, to play in a major tournament at home would be special," said the Brentford keeper.

"But I don't think we can think too far ahead into that. Obviously we've got to focus on tomorrow and trying to get a good result and we'll look towards that then when it comes.

"But we all know the opportunity that's there for us if we can perform, so it'll be a great opportunity."

#808. Taylor Swift Scores Five Grammy Nominations, Including Album and Record of the Year Nods

Swift‘s 'The Life of a Showgirl' album and track for 'Toy Story 5' are among the nominations for the February 2027 show.

Taylor Swift is headed to the 2027 Grammy Awards as a five-time nominee.

Swift received five nominations including record of the year for “The Fate of Ophelia“ and album of the year for The Life of a Showgirl. The Life of a Showgirl title track, which Swift performs with Sabrina Carpenter, is up for best pop duo/group performance. Meanwhile, her Toy Story 5 composition “I Knew It, I Knew You“ was nominated in the song of the year and best song written for visual media categories.

During the livestream of the Grammy nominations, Swift made a surprise appearance to announce the last two categories, album and song of the year. Related Stories Music 2027 Grammy Nominations: Raye, Rosalía Lead a Women-Dominated General Field Music Grammy Nominations: Watch the Livestream

Last year, the singer-songwriter went home empty-handed despite receiving six nominations, including album of the year and best pop vocal album for The Tortured Poets Department.

Swift has already made Grammys history after winning the coveted the album of the year Grammy four times. Swift won album of the year for her albums Fearless in 2010 — she surpassed Alanis Morissette as the category’s youngest victor at 20 years old — 1989 in 2015, folklore in 2021 and Midnights in 2024.

Swift and Adele are the only women to have taken home an award in this category more than once, with Adele winning for albums 21 and 25. Meanwhile, Frank Sinatra, Stevie Wonder and Paul Simon have also won the album of the year award three times.

For Swift‘s The Life of a Showgirl, which was recorded in between show dates during the European leg of her record-breaking Eras tour, the superstar reteamed with producers Max Martin and Shellback, who worked with Swift on some of her biggest pop hits, including “Shake It Off,” “Blank Space” and “I Knew You Were Trouble.” She first revealed the project on Travis and Jason Kelce’s New Heights podcast in August 2025. Just weeks after making the surprise announcement, Swift and Kelce revealed their engagement. The couple got married in July of this year.

Swift‘s “I Knew It, I Knew You“ marked a return to Swift’s country music roots with the singer-songwriter set to make her return to the CMA Awards stage after last performing there 13 years ago. The song, which has been considered a top contender for a song of the year Oscar nomination, is nominated for single of the year at the upcoming CMAs.

For the 2027 Grammys, female acts make up the leading nominees with Raye topping the nominations with 11 followed by Rosalía with nine; Ella Langley, Miranda Lambert, Olivia Rodrigo and Phoebe Bridgers with seven each; and Olivia Dean with six nods, tied with Bruno Mars and Leon Thomas.

Dolly Parton was posthumously nominated for three Grammys. Hollywood names including Michael J. Fox and the late Tim Curry scored nominations for best audiobook, narration and storytelling recording for their memoirs Future Boy and Vagabond: A Memoir, respectively. Comedians Nikki Glaser, Trevor Noah, Wanda Sykes, Fred Armisen, Jeff Ross and Dave Chappelle received noms in the best comedy album category.

The Grammys are also set to honor the best compilation soundtrack for visual media with nominees including The Devil Wears Prada 2 (various artists), Stranger Things Season 5 (various artists), Wicked: For Good (various artists), The Wizard of Oz at Sphere and Wuthering Heights (Charli XCX).

Ludwig Goransson scored two noms for best score soundtrack for visual media, a category that honors the composer, for The Odyssey and Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu.

This year’s eligibility period includes recordings released from Aug. 31, 2025, through Aug. 28, 2026. Final round voting, in which Recording Academy voting members choose the Grammy winners, will take place between Dec. 10, 2026 and Jan. 7, 2027.

The 2027 Grammys will air on ABC, marking the first time in more than 50 years that the music awards show hasn’t aired on its longtime home of CBS. The ceremony will premiere live across ABC, Disney+ and Hulu from Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles on Sunday, Feb. 7, 2027, at 7 p.m. ET / 4 p.m. PT.

The Telecast will be produced by Fulwell Entertainment for the Recording Academy, with Ben Winston, Raj Kapoor and Jesse Collins serving as executive producers.

Swift was also recently announced as the recipient of The Hollywood Reporter‘s prestigious Sherry Lansing Leadership Award, which she’ll accept at THR‘s 2026 Women in Entertainment gala.

#807. Burnham urges caution on scrapping 3pm TV blackout

The blackout originated in the 1960s when Burnley chairman Bob Lord encouraged the EFL to oppose television coverage of 15:00 Saturday matches

Andy Burnham has urged caution on lifting the Saturday 3pm TV blackout in the UK, saying the health of the football pyramid should come first.

The rule was introduced in the 1960s to encourage fans to attend lower league games and prevents matches from being shown on UK television between 2:45pm and 5:15pm on Saturdays.

The blackout, which is enforced by Article 48 of the Uefa Statutes and is imposed by the English and Scottish football associations, comes into effect when 50% of fixtures in the top two divisions are scheduled to kick off at 3pm.

The Premier League is in the middle of a record Â£6.7bn domestic TV deal for Sky and TNT to show up to 270 live games a season.

But there could be room for change with the 3pm rule in the upcoming broadcast cycle, as the rights deals for the Premier League, EFL and SPFL all end in 2028-29.

The prime minister said any decision to remove the ban would require careful thought about the consequences.

"I would urge a bit of caution [on the blackout], because it does protect the income of lower-league clubs," Burnham said.

Scottish football could pave way for 3pm TV blackout to end

Why does football have Saturday 3pm TV blackout in UK?

"If you have effectively wall-to-wall Premier League football at any time, it takes away perhaps the incentive to go and watch the football league or non-league.

"So I think it has to be considered carefully. I'm not going to take the pure consumer view here. I'll take the health-of-football approach to this particular issue."

Only the FA Cup final, which traditionally kicks off at 3pm, is allowed to be broadcast during the blackout window.

In October, the SPFL said it is "flexible about the number of games" that will form part of the TV new deal, which BBC Sport understands includes matches shown on a Saturday afternoon.

Premier League chief executive Richard Masters has previously said a decision about whether the blackout stays in place would need to be made in the future.

But Burnham added: "I would first of all want to protect the football pyramid before I agree to saying 'let's have even more live football'".

"I think it's about protecting the experience with the paying supporter, protecting the football pyramid. Those issues matter to me, first of all."

#806. Belgium's Lukaku retires from internationals

Romelu Lukaku scored three goals for Belgium at the World Cup this summer

Romelu Lukaku has retired from international football, saying he has "enjoyed every single moment" of playing for Belgium.

Fenerbahce striker Lukaku, 33, made his international debut in 2010 and is Belgium's all-time leading men's goalscorer with 94 goals in 135 appearances.

He is the fifth highest men's international goalscorer of all time, behind Sunil Chhetri, Ali Daei, Lionel Messi and leader Cristiano Ronaldo, who has scored 146.

Lukaku scored eight goals across four World Cups, including in the run to the quarter-finals at this summer's tournament, and a total of six goals at three European Championships.

Writing on Instagram,, external the former Everton, Chelsea and Manchester United forward thanked his team-mates and coaches "for pushing and trusting me to help the team" during his 16 years with the national side.

He missed Belgium's Nations League win over Turkey last week with a hip injury and was an unused substitute on Sunday as they qualified for the last eight of the competition by beating Italy 4-1.

"These 16 years I gave all I had for the national team... I went through every emotion possible," Lukaku wrote.

"To the Belgium fans thank you for the support you gave our team. I am proud to have represented my country in four World Cups and three European Championships.

"I will never forget those moments. I'm at peace with my decision to stop here. It was amazing. It was enjoyable. I'm grateful."

In 2023, Lukaku scored 14 times in eight Euro 2024 qualifying appearances, breaking the record for goals scored by a player in a European Championship qualifying campaign.

His Belgium team-mate Kevin de Bruyne posted an image of himself with Lukaku, external on Instagram adding: "There are no words to describe what you've meant to me and our country!"

#805. Dolly Parton Lands Three Posthumous Grammy Nominations

With the reveal of the 2027 Grammy nominations on Monday, Parton now has 58 total noms.

Dolly Parton has been posthumously nominated for three Grammy Awards.

The “Jolene” singer received two nods in the best country duo/group performance; the first stemming from her feature on Zac Brown’s “Butterfly,” with the second hailing from her song “Light of a Clear Blue Morning” with Lainey Wilson, Miley Cyrus, Queen Latifah and Reba McEntire.

Parton’s third nomination is for best audiobook, narration and storytelling recording, tied to her 2025 memoir Star of the Show: My Life on Stage. Related Stories Music 2027 Grammy Nominations: Raye, Rosalía Lead a Women-Dominated General Field Music Grammy Nominations: Watch the Livestream

With the reveal of the 2027 Grammy nominations on Monday, Parton now has 58 total noms. She has previously won 10 Grammys, and received the Recording Academy’s Lifetime Achievement Award in 2011. Additionally, her songs “Jolene” and “I Will Always Love You” have been inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame.

Parton died Aug. 25, after a “brief battle with cancer,” a rep announced. She was 80. Her death led to an outpouring of tributes from the entertainment industry, from the likes of Miley Cyrus, Taylor Swift, Billy Ray Cyrus, Jane Fonda, Celine Dion and many more.

Harvey Mason Jr., CEO of the Grammys and MusiCares, commended Parton in a statement shared with The Hollywood Reporter at the time of her death.

“It’s nearly impossible to fully capture the depth of what Dolly Parton means to the world. She was a 10-time Grammy winner, a recipient of the Recording Academy’s Lifetime Achievement Award and the 2019 MusiCares Person of the Year honoree, but reducing her legacy to accolades doesn’t do justice to what she truly represented: love, kindness and generosity on a scale that transcended music,” Mason Jr. wrote.

Parton was honored with a tribute at the 2025 Emmys led by McEntire and Sally Field.
