#804. Cap fits as Robertson poised to take King Kenny's crown

You've done Liverpool and Scotland proud - Kenny Dalglish on Andy Robertson's career

Andy Robertson will become the most capped men's Scotland international if he earns his 103rd cap in Monday night's Nations League campaign closer in Switzerland.

Twelve years on from his debut - off the bench in a Poland friendly - he is set to surpass his friend and fellow Liverpool legend, Kenny Dalglish, whose record haul has stood for 40 years.

On moving level with the man they - and he - will always call King, the Tottenham Hotspur left-back shifted chat towards the former forward, his commendable humility laid bare.

But, in St Gallen, the spotlight will be brightly shone on one of Scotland's favourite sons as he goes solo at the summit.

Robertson set to make history, but hero Dalglish will always be King

Inside the fairytale journey of Scotland captain Robertson

Andy Robertson on his hero, Kenny Dalglish

For much of this year, Dalglish was the only man to have pulled on the navy blue of Scotland more times than Robertson.

'King Kenny' topped the list on 102 caps - earning his last in November 1986 against Luxembourg when in a player-manager role at Liverpool.

Few since have even come close to toppling him - even when Robertson does, he is keen to stress the throne is still reserved for Dalglish - but it is perhaps fitting it is the current captain, given their great friendship.

Which allows Dalglish to say he's not having any of it.

"He always says: 'You've got millions more games. Nations League, what's that? They didn't have that in my day!'" Robertson joked on the Stick to Football podcast recently.

"I think he might bring up a ratio for years-to-games-played so he's still on top.

"It's obviously something that's been on my radar for a while now. When you get to 80-odd caps, you start to look up."

Dalglish can console himself that his record of 30 goals - held jointly with Denis Law - is safely out of Robertson's reach.

But not out of John McGinn's - the midfielder's double against North Macedonia on Friday having taken him to within six of the legendary duo.

The Aston Villa captain is lurking only eight caps behind Robertson on the all-time caps list, too, so the Scotland men's centurion club could have three members soon.

Since being given the armband by Alex McLeish after Scott Brown retired in 2018, Robertson has captained Scotland 32 times more than any other player.

At the time, he had earned just 22 caps and was just 24 but had established himself as Liverpool's left-back as they reached the Champions League final.

Now he is the only man to have led Scotland out at three major finals, reaching the milestone at the World Cup this summer.

Scotland and Napoli midfielder Scott McTominay enthused: "He's such a great captain and he's got that good balance between being one of the senior players and saying you need to wake up if you're not playing well.

"Then he's also got the personable side, organising things with the manager, helping young players and stuff. He's brilliant with that, brilliant."

One of those young players is 20-year-old Findlay Curtis, who told the media the night before Robertson's potentially-historic night that his captain has "probably been the biggest role model" he's looked up to since joining the international set-up earlier this year.

Perhaps that was because Robertson did him a turn back in the day. Unbeknownst to the skipper.

Rangers winger Curtis was only 14 during the Covid pandemic and was partial to playing a bit of Fifa, and Robertson was a star in his team.

"I was just thinking, I had him in my Fifa team," he explained. "[For] defending and he was just fast as well.

"What a servant he has been for the country."

'I had him in my Fifa team!' - Findlay Curtis on going from fan to team-mate of Robertson

Robertson has played under four permanent Scotland team bosses in his 12-year international career.

It was Strachan who plucked him from the under-21s to hand him his debut as a 19-year-old in a win over Poland in March 2014.

McLeish made him captain in 2018, calling Robertson the "outstanding candidate" and an "inspirational figure" - and now he has played five times for new boss Sebastien Pocognoli.

He even played one game under interim manager Malky Mackay in a friendly against the Netherlands at Pittodrie in 2017 as the Scottish FA searched for Strachan's replacement.

However, it is Steve Clarke's seven-year stint that Robertson will be mainly associated with, as the pair led Scotland to three major tournaments.

Robertson played 68 times for Clarke, all of them as captain, and the recently departed head coach consistently praised his figurehead.

"He's been a fantastic captain for Scotland," Clarke said at the World Cup.

"He's worked ever so hard for the country and he leads the group like the leader he is - and he's very, very important to me and the squad."

Over the piece, Robertson's caps are spread fairly evenly among friendlies and qualification games.

Crucially, though, he has also played nine times in major tournaments. What will rankle with him is there is only one win among those nine - June's victory over Haiti in Boston at the World Cup.

Overall, though, Robertson's Scotland career can be characterised by consistency.

He has started 100 of his 102 caps, rarely ever being substituted. He has not missed a camp in three years.

The only question seems to be how many Scotland caps will Robertson end up with?

At 32 and still playing in the Premier League, it appears there will be plenty more to come.

#803. Grammys: Michael J. Fox, Tim Curry, ‘Wicked: For Good,’ ‘The Pitt’ Among Hollywood Nominees

The 2027 noms were revealed Monday morning.

Several Hollywood names were among the nominees for the 2027 Grammy Awards, which were announced Monday morning.

Michael J. Fox and the late Tim Curry scored nominations for best audiobook, narration and storytelling recording for their memoirs Future Boy and Vagabond: A Memoir, respectively. Fox is already a Grammy winner, having taken home the award for best spoken word album for Always Looking Up: The Adventures of an Incurable Optimist in 2010. Curry, who died in August, previously received a nom in that same category, for narrating A Series of Unfortunate Events – Book 1: The Bad Beginning, but has never won. They’ll vie with Michelle Obama for The Look, Paul McCartney and Morgan Neville for The Man on the Run, Lil Jon for Remix Meditation and the late Dolly Parton for Star of the Show: My Life on Stage. Related Stories Music Dolly Parton Lands Three Posthumous Grammy Nominations Music Taylor Swift Scores Five Grammy Nominations, Including Album and Record of the Year Nods

The Grammy for best comedy album also saw several Hollywood comedians land noms. The nominees are Nikki Glaser for Good Girl, Trevor Noah for Joy in the Trenches, Wanda Sykes for Legacy, Fred Armisen for 100 Sound Effects, Jeff Ross for Take a Banana for the Ride and Dave Chappelle for The Unstoppable. All have received Grammy nominees in the past except for first-timer Ross. Chappelle has won in this category six times previously.

The Grammys also honor the best compilation soundtrack for visual media, where several shows and movies landed noms, including The Devil Wears Prada 2 (various artists), Stranger Things Season 5 (various artists), Wicked: For Good (various artists), The Wizard of Oz at Sphere and Wuthering Heights (Charli XCX).

Ludwig Göransson scored two noms for best score soundtrack for visual media, a category that honors the composer, for The Odyssey and Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu. He’ll vie with Jonny Greenwood for One Battle After Another, Daniel Pemberton for Project Hail Mary and David Fleming for Widow’s Bay.

The Grammys also honor songs written specifically for film, TV, video games and other visual media, an award that goes to the songwriter. The nominees in that category include “House” from Wuthering Heights (John Cale and Charli XCX), “I Knew It, I Knew You” from Toy Story 5 (Jack Antonoff and Taylor Swift), “Need Someone” from The Pitt (Andrew Bird), “No Place Like Home” from Wicked: For Good and “Runway” from the The Devil Wears Prada 2 (Henry Walter, Jaylah Hickmon, Dernst “D’Mile” Emile II, Stefani Germanotta, Jayda Love, Bruno Mars and Andrew Watt).

The Recording Academy announced nominees for the 69th Grammy Awards in 101 categories, including five new awards: best Asian pop music performance, best R&B collaboration or duo/group performance, best traditional pop vocal performance, best traditional folk album and best Latin song.

Grammys CEO Harvey Mason Jr. and Recording Academy Board of Trustees chair Dr. Chelsey Green were joined by Grammy-winning and -nominated artists including Alan Menken, Amy Allen, Carly Pearce, David Guetta, FYÜTCH & Aura V, Herbie Hancock, Israel Houghton, Juanes, Kehlani, Linda Perry, Meghan Foley & Michelle Holme, Olivia Dean, Pharrell Williams, Renée Fleming, YUNGBLUD and Ziggy Marley in announcing the 2027 Grammy nominees.

The 2027 Grammy Awards will air live from Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles on Feb. 7, 2027, and simulcast across ABC, Disney+ and Hulu. A host has not yet been announced. This year’s Grammy eligibility period is Aug. 31, 2025-Aug. 28, 2026.

#802. Klopp says Infantino worse than Blatter

Jurgen Klopp took over as Germany head coach in July

Germany manager Jurgen Klopp says he "didn't think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter, but someone has managed to do just that" as he called for Fifa president Gianni Infantino to be replaced.

Blatter resigned as Fifa boss in 2015 amid a corruption scandal and was succeeded by Infantino in February 2016.

Infantino plans to stand for re-election in March but has been under pressure since scrapping his Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, which included selling off stakes in the World Cup and other Fifa competitions to private investors.

Infantino apologised to the Fifa Council for the plan but was told he was not fit to lead world football's governing body unless he released all the documents and answered key questions.

"I've been following football for many years. There are people who are much more knowledgeable about this than I am. But I think most people now agree a change would make a lot of sense," said Klopp.

"I didn't think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter, but someone has managed to do just that."

Klopp added: "Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job."

Wenger decides not to challenge Fifa chief Infantino

Infantino apologises to Fifa Council - but told he is still not fit to lead

Uefa - European football's governing body - has been one of Infantino's fiercest critics and has repeatedly called on him to stand down.

It has prepared criminal legal proceedings against Infantino and lodged a claim in three US courts for all documents related to FFE to be released.

The deadline for candidates to officially confirm they are standing against Infantino in Fifa's presidential election is Wednesday.

Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger, who is Fifa's head of global development, had been considering running for the job but sources have told BBC Sport he has ruled himself out.

Uefa is said to still be hopeful of finding an alternative candidate before Wednesday's deadline.

Former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega was the first person to put his name forward in October.

Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima has also announced his intention to stand.

"There are people who truly care about the future of football - people who aren't driven by financial interests," said Klopp.

"If someone like that were to step up - if someone like that were to become president - I think that would be a significant improvement.

"There are surely people who care deeply about the future of football and have no financial interests in it."

#801. Why Taylor Swift's Showgirl Encore Album Isn’t Eligible for Grammys

Though Taylor Swift’s “Patient Zero” broke records this year, the song and its album The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore aren’t eligible for the 2027 Grammys because of the Recording Academy’s rules.

Taylor Swift’s latest album won’t go in the blank space of Grammys ballots.

That’s because The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore—the deluxe version of her The Life of a Showgirl album—doesn’t qualify for the 2027 Grammys for multiple reasons.

First, for a song or album to be eligible for the upcoming Grammys, which will be handed out in February 2027, it would have needed to be released within the eligibility window of Aug. 31, 2025, to Aug. 28, 2026.

But since the extended version of Swift’s album was released on Sept. 25, it falls outside of eligibility for the 2027 Grammys.

But even the following year, the Encore album, with its four new songs, still won’t be eligible for Album of the Year if rules remain the same. That’s because the Grammys’ Recording Academy now requires that new recordings make up at least 66 percent of an album—a decrease from the previous threshold of 75 percent—in order to qualify.

But that worry you feel for Swift’s Grammy hopes? You can shake it off.

Her new tracks “Patient Zero,” “Pink Clouding,” “Babylon” and “Cleveland!” will be eligible for consideration at the 2028 show for categories that recognize individual songs.

And of course, the original Life of a Showgirl album—released in October 2025—is up for all categories at the 2027 Grammys.

Meanwhile, Swift’s song “I Knew It, I Knew You,” which she wrote for Toy Story 5, isn’t just collecting teardrops on the guitars of fans—it could also bring home trophies for Song of the Year, Best Song Written for Visual Media, Best Country Song, Best Country Solo Performance and other categories, if nominated.

“Writing this song felt like a musical departure and coming home at the same time,” the “Anti-Hero” singer wrote on Instagram in June. “Creating something for Jessie was a new challenge and also felt like second nature all at once.”

She also shared her appreciation for the movie’s director, adding, “Thank you to the brilliant Andrew Stanton for imagining me for this, all those years ago when you wrote this newest film.”

To learn what—and who—inspired many of Swift’s other songs, keep reading…

Before The Life of a Showgirl, the only track Taylor had certainly written about her guy on the Chiefs—save for The Eras Tour “Karma” rewrite, of course—is “So High School,” which the now-engaged couple aptly set their proposal Instagram post to in August 2025.

Although some fans speculate “The Alchemy,” also off The Tortured Poets Department, is about Travis for the football and high school metaphors sprinkled in the track, “So High School” includes a more obvious nod with the lyrics: “Are you going to marry, kiss or kill me? / It’s just a game but really / I’m betting on all three, for us two.”

Indeed, Travis revealed to AfterBuzzTV back in 2016 that “Taylor Swift, would be the kiss,” in a game of “Marry, Kiss, Kill” between her, Ariana Grande and Katy Perry.

As for how Travis feels about the track? Although it’s a tough competition as a Swiftie, it’s his all-time favorite.

“I’m not gonna lie,” he joked of the choice to Access Hollywood in 2024. “I might be a little biased.”

But now that Taylor has found the guy who can call her honey, he's the one she most wants to pay tribute to in verse.

On The Life of a Showgirl, she sang about her now-husband topping her "Wi$h Li$t," serving as her "forever night stand" in "Honey," and turning her sky "Opalite."

And, forgive her, it sounds cocky, but in "Wood," her raciest song yet, she shared how Travis' love was the key that opened her thighs.

Fortunately, Taylor's mom Andrea Swift, "thinks that the song is about superstitions, which it absolutely is," Taylor joked on SiriusXM’s Morning Mash Up after the album's October 2025 release. "That’s the joy of the double entendre. You can read that song for people, and it just goes right over their heads."

But it wasn't hard to grasp who she was calling "the love of my life" on the Encore track "Cleveland!," the title itself an overt nod to Travis' hometown.

Although short-lived, Taylor appeared to write several songs on The Tortured Poets Department about her dalliance with The 1975 frontman in 2023, including the album’s title track which also name drops their mutual pal and collaborator Jack Antonoff.

Other tracks rumored to be about Matty include “Fortnight,” “Down Bad,” and “But Daddy I Love Him,” the latter of which also appears to call out the backlash Taylor received for her relationship with him.

And while Matty told paparazzi, per Entertainment Tonight in 2024 that he hadn’t listened to the album, though he was "sure it’s good," his mother Denise Welch slammed his alleged connection to the breakup ballads.

"You're not allowed to say anything," the Loose Woman cohost said during a 2025 appearance on Watch What Happens Live, "and then she writes a whole album about it."

For more on Matty’s place in Taylor’s catalogue, read here.

It's actually sweet all the time an unnamed rival has spent on the singer. Or, at least, that's what Taylor conveyed in The Life of a Showgirl track "Actually Romantic."

Rather than share her praise for Travis or even an ex-lover, the musician actually sings about a person who "high-fived my ex and then you said you're glad he ghosted me. Wrote me a song saying it makes you sick to see my face / Some people might be offended / But it's actually sweet."

Fans were quick to say the clues pointed toward Charli XCX, who opened for Taylor on her Reputation Tour and is close with Taylor's ex Matty and his now-wife Gabbriette Bechtel.

Another tell was Charli's 2024 brat track "Sympathy Is a Knife," in which the British musician—married to Matty's The 1975 bandmate George Daniel—sings, "Don’t wanna see her backstage at my boyfriend’s show. Fingers crossed behind my back / I hope they break up real quick."

Good thing for Brittany Mahomes, Taylor likes her friends canceled. Because fans feel the singer was thinking of the former soccer player—wed to Travis' teammate Patrick Mahomes—or onetime BFF Blake Lively when she wrote about standing by a pal's side when the whole world has seemingly turned on them.

But really the person at the crux of The Life of a Showgirl track is Taylor herself, who felt her reputation took several hits after her very public 2016 feud with Kanye West and then-wife Kim Kardashian.

"Having had my own experiences with mass judgment and being at the center of many dramatic, scandalous moments in my career, where people were all weighing in at once or at least it felt like that," she told Amazon Music, "having had those experiences, it makes me move through the world a little bit differently."

And now she wants to gift that what-doesn't-kill-you-makes-you-stronger mentality to others. As the lyrics suggest, Taylor continued, "I don't just naturally cast people aside just because other people decide they don't like them. I make my own decisions about people based on how they treat me within my life and their actions."

Amid their six-year relationship, Taylor penned several songs about—and with—the Conversations With Friends star. Shortly after the pair's relationship was confirmed in 2016, she released Reputation, which included several songs presumably about Joe such as “Call It What You Want,” “Dress,” and “King of My Heart.”

On Lover, Taylor also included the track "Cornelia Street," a nod to the New York City rental she was living in during the early months of their romance. Elsewhere in her discography, fans believe Taylor also penned "invisible string," on folklore about her romance with Joe, as well as Midnights' "Sweet Nothing" and its bonus track 'You’re Losing Me," which her producer Jack confirmed was written two years before Taylor's 2023 breakup with Joe.

Joe is one of the many people in Taylor’s life who has also become her cowriter on songs, earning credits on folklore and evermore songs like "betty," "champagne problems," "exile" and others under the pseudonym William Bowery.

"It was really the most accidental thing to happen in lockdown," the Brutalist alum told GQ of the cowriting credits in 2022. "It was just messing around on a piano and singing badly and being overheard and then thinking, you know, what if we tried to get to the end of it together?"

For more songs inspired by Joe, see here.

Following the infamous—and later revealed to be edited—phone call leak in 2016 between Kanye and Taylor over a reference he made to her on his The Life of Pablo album, Taylor has subtly clapped back at the divorced couple more than once.

As recently as 2024, Taylor penned "thanK you aIMee" likely about Kim, given she capitalized letters in the track's title to spell out her name. (In another variant of the TTPD album, she changed the letters to capitalize "YE" in the track, as an apparent nod toward the rapper.)

Prior to TTPD, Taylor also sprinkled hits against Kim and Kanye for the "Famous" feud, with "Mad Woman," on folklore, where she sings, "Women like hunting witches too / Doing your dirtiest work for you / It’s obvious that wanting me dead has really brought you two together."

Taylor’s first Reputation single "Look What You Made Me Do," was also a nod to the public fallout, as well as "This Is Why We Can’t Have Nice Things," in which she sings about a once-repaired friendship fracturing again.

But, of course, Taylor's musical inspirations from Kanye date back to that 2009 MTV VMA incident, when he interrupted her speech for Best Female Video at the Video Music Awards. In Speak Now’s "Innocent," she forgives Kanye for the viral moment, which earned him backlash from figures as prominent as then-president Barack Obama.

"It's OK / Life is a tough crowd," Taylor sings on the track, going on to reference his age at the time of the VMAs. "32 and still growing up now / Who you are is not what you did / You’re still an innocent."

For a thorough dive into Taylor’s beef with Kanye, see here.

Taylor and the Loki actor may have only had a short-lived romance in the summer of 2016, but it did inspire more than one track for the "Karma" singer. Indeed, many fans speculated that "Getaway Car," and "High Infidelity" are about the timeline of their romance in comparison to her relationship with Calvin Harris. She and the DJ split in June 2016 after one year of dating, the same month she sparked rumors with Tom.

In both songs, Taylor sings about how a relationship born out of slight infidelity is doomed from the start.

While fans are sure these three are the ones who made up the "Getaway Car" sideshow, neither Taylor, nor Calvin or Tom have addressed the inspiration for the songs.

Although Taylor shut down any speculation that she wrote songs about her romance with the One Direction alum, there are a lot of subtle references to the "Watermelon Sugar" singer on 1989.

"Style," is the most obvious nod to Harry, simply for the title, as well as "Out of the Woods," and bonus track "Wonderland," which references a "Cheshire cat smile"—which many fans see as a nod to Harry’s hometown of Holmes Chapel in Cheshire, England.

Meanwhile, the 1989 vault track "Is It Over Now?" paints a vivid picture of the moment Taylor knew her romance with Harry was done for good.

"Blue dress on a boat," she sings in reference to the infamous January 2013 photo of her after the couple’s alleged breakup in the Virgin Islands. "Your new girl is my clone."

On "Now That We Don’t Talk," she references the doomed vacation again, and slams Harry’s infamous music taste in the lines, "I don’t have to pretend I like acid rock / Or that I’d like to be on a mega-yacht."

And while Taylor went on to date several more stars from across the pond, Harry was her first British bloke. And since London is referenced in other songs in her earlier catalogue, including Red’s "Come Back, Be Here" and "Message in a Bottle," the tracks are also speculated to be about Harry.

Harry didn’t earn the entirety of 1989’s inspiration. Indeed, many fans believe the track "Bad Blood" is about Katy as Taylor teased to Rolling Stone in 2014 it was about another "female artist," who "tried to sabotage an entire arena tour."

"I was like, 'Oh, we’re just straight-up enemies,'" Taylor, who at the time saw some of her background dancers leave for Katy's Prismatic tour, added. "It wasn’t even about a guy! It had to do with business."

However, Taylor maintained she penned the song simply to get some feelings off her chest.

"My intent was not to create some gossip-fest," she added to Rolling Stone. "I wanted people to apply it to a situation where they felt betrayed in their own lives."

Ultimately, though, the song fueled a feud—with Katy posting on X one day after the Rolling Stone piece published, "Watch out for Regina George in sheep’s clothing."

The singers were later able to squash their beef in 2019, after which Katy made a cameo in Taylor’s "You Need to Calm Down" music video.

Taylor can write fanfiction, too. Ahead of the release of Red, Taylor met Ethel while dating her grandson Conor Kennedy, and ultimately penned the song "Starlight" about a reimagined version of a date night between the Kennedy matriarch and her late husband.

"Starlight is a song that I wrote after seeing a picture of Ethel and Bobby Kennedy when they were 17," Taylor explained in a Red interview. "I didn’t know anything about what they were doing or what was going on in the picture, but I just thought 'They look like they’re having the best night.' And so I wrote this song about what the night might’ve been like."

In response to the nod, Ethel told the Cape Cod Times, "She is just sensational, inside and out."

One of Taylor’s most popular breakup songs of all time "All Too Well"—and its 10-minute alternate version—is thought to be about the Donnie Darko star. After all, it references autumn—when their short-lived 2010 romance took place—her subject’s sister’s house, and a certain scarf. (Jake, of course, has a very famous sister in Maggie Gyllenhaal, and the duo passed a striped Gucci scarf between them during their romance.)

Taylor also appeared to take shots at her romance with Jake in "The Last Time," "We Are Never Getting Back Together," and the Red vault track "I Bet You Think About Me," which call out the subject’s music taste and wealthy background.

Despite widespread belief Red as a whole was mostly inspired by Jake, he shut down any connection following the album’s 2021 rerelease.

"It’s about her relationship with her fans," he told Esquire in 2022. "It is her expression."

Taylor, meanwhile, did concur with Jake's sentiment, noting that she saw "All Too Well" become something much deeper than a breakup song.

"What was so crazy is that when it went out into the world, the fans just among themselves decided it was their favorite too," she explained on Good Morning America in 2021.  "They just sort of ... claimed it as the most important song from Red...over the course of the first six months the album was out."

Many fans speculate that The Tortured Poets Department's "The Manuscript" is about the impact of "All Too Well," and thus, Taylor's relationship with Jake.

Yes, at least half of Taylor’s heart—at the age of 19, anyway—once belonged to the "Gravity" musician. And it possibly led to some of her Speak Now tracks like "Dear John," and "The Story of Us," which Taylor previously revealed were inspired by the same person.

"'The Story of Us' is about running into someone I had been in a relationship with at an awards show, and we were seated a few seats away from each other," she told USA Today in 2010. "I just wanted to say to him, 'Is this killing you? Because it's killing me.' But I didn't. Because I couldn't. Because we both had these silent shields up."

While Taylor has said she doesn’t use Easter eggs to hint at her personal life, the "Story of Us" liner notes—where Taylor used to hide messages for her fans—on the original Speak Now album spelled out "CMT Awards," an event she and John both attended in 2010.

As for where "Dear John" is concerned? John himself had to respond to the brazen shots fired.

"I didn’t deserve it," the musician told Rolling Stone in 2012. "I'm pretty good at taking accountability now, and I never did anything to deserve that. It was a really lousy thing for her to do."

Once too young to be messed with, Taylor is now too wise to be bothered with any drama. "I don’t care about anything that happened to me when I was 19," she told fans ahead of playing "Dear John," at The Eras Tour in 2023. "Except for the songs that I wrote and the memories we made together."

As she put it, “I do not care. We’ve all grown up. We’re good.”

Following a 2009 romance with the Twilight star, Taylor penned "Back to December" about the relationship. In addition to alluding to a "September night" where her subject saw her cry (Lautner was also at the 2009 VMAs), she included a nod to him in the song’s liner notes, which read, "Tay."

Ahead of Speak Now's rerelease in 2023, the Sharkboy and Lava Girl alum joked about his role in the album’s songs, telling Today at the time, "I feel safe."

Some fans also speculate that "Today Was a Fairytale" and "I Can See You"—the music video he starred in—were about her Valentine’s Day costar as well, as in the latter track, Taylor sings about keeping "everything professional," before a romance ensued.

Believe it or not, Taylor once got butterflies from the "Fireflies" singer. "Enchanted" is about a night she met the frontman for Owl City, and she revealed she included the line "wonderstruck" so he’d know it was about him, as he had used the word in an email to her.

"Meeting him," Taylor told Yahoo in 2010. "It was this overwhelming feeling of: I really hope that you’re not in love with somebody."

A year later, Adam responded to the musical love letter by rerecording the song, adding in his own lyrics, "Oh Taylor, I was so enchanted to meet you too."

"I'll be the first to admit I’m a rather shy boy and since music is the most eloquent form of communication I can muster, I decided to record something for you–a sort of a 'reply' to the breathtaking song on your current record," he added in a note beneath the song, shared to his band's website at the time. "You are a true princess from a dreamy fairy tale."

Once upon a time, Taylor was extremely up front when it came to who inspired her songs, especially where her breakup with Joe Jonas is concerned. Back in 2008, she quickly penned "Forever and Always" and tacked it on as a last-minute addition to Fearless, perfectly timed to her infamous appearance on Ellen, where she called out the Jonas Brothers member for breaking up with her in a 27-second phone call.

On her next album, Speak Now, released in 2010, Taylor included two nods to Joe, including "Last Kiss," a heart-wrenching ballad which references July 9, a.k.a. the date of the 2008 Jonas Brothers concert she attended while she and Joe were still together.

Elsewhere on the album, Taylor included "Better Than Revenge," which was a clap back at the Jonas Brothers’ song "Much Better," which had a not-so-veiled reference to her in the lyric, "I'm done with superstars and all the tears on her guitar."

Later on in her discography, Taylor included fonder nods to her past romance with Joe on Red’s "Holy Ground," and folklore’s "Invisible String," the latter in which she reflects on becoming friendly with him in more recent years. "Cold was the steel of my axe to grind for the boys who broke my heart," she sings in the song, "Now I send their babies presents."

However, when Taylor released Fearless (Taylor’s Version) in 2021, she gave Joe one more whack with "Mr. Perfectly Fine," though she penned the song around the time of their 2008 breakup. It was Joe’s now-ex-wife Sophie Turner who seemingly confirmed the track was about her then-husband, sharing the song to social media at the time and joking, "It's not NOT a bop."

#800. Apple TV Bulks Up With Video Podcasts

Video podcasts that are available via the Apple Podcasts app will now be available to watch within the Apple TV app, and users can pick up where they left off regardless of which app they use.

Video podcasts are coming to Apple TV, as the tech giant links together its Apple Podcasts and Apple TV app in a unique setup that only it could deliver.

The change will bring video shows from Apple Podcasts to the Apple TV app, with no subscription required. Notably, users will be able to move seamlessly between the apps, letting them pick up where they left off regardless of which app or which device they were watching on.

Apple says that in the last three months the number of podcasts publishing video to its platform has doubled, while the video episode catalogue has tripled. The company says that top podcasts that had video episodes saw a 20 percent viewing boost, on average.

The Apple TV news means that video podcast creators now have significantly more reach than they had exclusively through the podcast app, particularly on TV sets where the Apple TV app is more likely to live.

It also gives Apple TV a significantly larger pool of video content, helping it more effectively compete in a crowded video app ecosystem. YouTube has become a dominant podcast platform by leaning into video, while other premium video platforms like Netflix and Disney+ have sought to acquire video podcasts to supplement their other content.

Apple, of course, is already a power player in the podcast space, now it is just using that muscle to help bolster other parts of its ecosystem.

#798. Has Trafford replaced Pickford as England No 1?

James Trafford has made five appearances for England, all of them in 2026

As he was mobbed by his England team-mates for a late double save that secured England's memorable 3-2 win against world champions Spain on Sunday, the debate that followed about who the country's number one is was inevitable.

The Leeds stopper was given his chance to show England boss Thomas Tuchel what he could do again - and he absolutely took it.

On his fifth England cap the 24-year-old enjoyed a magnificent performance in Madrid as his side handed the hosts their first loss in 43 matches.

Trafford made four key saves in the final 12 minutes of the game, including an incredible double stop to first deny a Lamine Yamal curler and then dive again to his right to keep out Fermin Lopez from close range.

Last week England manager Thomas Tuchel had made it clear that Everton goalkeeper Jordan Pickford was his number one.

But after full-time in Spain Tuchel told ITV Sport "there's no number one" and Trafford had "a brilliant match".

So, following his performance on Sunday night, is Trafford now likely to oust Pickford as England's go-to goalkeeper?

Is Trafford 'closing the gap' on Pickford?

Despite being just 24 years old Trafford has already been England's most expensive goalkeeper by transfer fee... twice.

Trafford returned to his boyhood Manchester City from Burnley for a Â£31m fee in 2025 and then left the Etihad for Leeds for Â£45m this summer - having been limited to being Pep Guardiola's 'cup goalkeeper'.

Given the downturn in form of their current goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma, many City fans may well be wishing Trafford had stayed. Their loss is Leeds' - and maybe England's - gain.

At Leeds he has found his form and this season ranks first among the 52 goalkeepers who have played at least 10 games in Europe's big five leagues by save percentage (81.4%).

He has made five appearances for England, all of them in 2026, and has rotated with Pickford across the Three Lions' five matches since the World Cup.

Pickford has started against Czech Republic and Croatia twice whereas Trafford has played against Czech Republic and started both England's matches with Spain, home and away.

After England's win in Madrid, which was the first time Spain had lost in the city in 39 years, Trafford's double-save was praised by his Three Lions team-mate Declan Rice.

"Everything happened so quick so for him to make two in the space of two seconds is massive," he told ITV. "A massive night for him."

Spain manager Luis de la Fuente agreed. He said: "We did generate some chances but England's goalkeeper has produced a fantastic performance and stopped two or three potential goals in the last 10 or 15 minutes."

After the double-save several England players ran over to celebrate with Trafford.

And on Tuchel's decision to rotate between his two keepers former Manchester United captain Roy Keane told ITV: "I think it's smart management.

"This is the perfect time for Trafford to come in, against top players, and show what he's capable of doing."

Social media has been full of the 'England number one' debate since, with many suggesting this was a moment that marked the changing of the guard.

Could Tuchel really now not start with Trafford for England's Nations League quarter-finals? Only time will tell.

What about Jordan Pickford though? England's undisputed first choice for almost 10 years has rarely let his country down.

Pickford, 32, has won 94 caps for England since making his debut in a 0-0 draw with Germany in 2017 and during his time as number one England have reached two World Cup semi-finals and two Euros finals.

According to Opta stats, Pickford has only made two errors leading to goals across his England career, with 46 clean sheets and a 74.3% save ratio.

And since the start of the 2024-25 season, only Arsenal's title-winning keeper David Raya has more clean sheets in the league than Pickford at Everton.

"We saw the last selections and all thought Jordan Pickford's place is under threat and James Trafford is going to be the next number one. I don't think Thomas Tuchel saw it as starkly or simply as that," said former England number one goalkeeper Paul Robinson to BBC Sport before England's win against Spain,

"It's a conversation that will definitely take place down the road, but not now. Jordan is England's first choice, in my opinion, rightfully so given his consistency and performances over such a long period.

"This is a debate and conversation for the future definitely because Father Time catches up with everyone eventually and the manager needs to have a contingency plan, but Jordan Pickford very much remains number one and Thomas Tuchel has said as much.

"I don't think Jordan Pickford is under threat for his jersey on a permanent basis any time soon, irrespective of the next selection."

This isn't a debate that is going away any time soon. But having two goalkeepers genuinely competing for that number one shirt can only be to England's benefit.

#797. Accept all changes

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Jiayi Zhao spends an unreasonable amount of time thinking about impossible worlds, difficult mathematics and who gets to count.

Mara had rejected 19 universes before lunch.

One contained faster-than-light rabbits. Eight ended with humanity finding itself living in a simulation. The nineteenth came to 940 words, but only because the title, biography and copyright notices were also counted.

Submission No. 1604490 seemed different. It arrived as a world.

Three machine intelligences were listed on the cover sheet: ORIGON-57, Blue Oak and ∫Stellaria. Their story opened on a planet where shadows migrated north each winter, leaving their owners wondering whether to follow. Elegant. Restrained. Also, scientifically impossible in exactly the right way.

Mara read to the last snowfall. Her cursor passed “RECOMMEND REJECTION” — almost muscle memory — and “ACCEPT ALL CHANGES”, which she had never used. She pressed “RECOMMEND ACCEPTANCE”.

Machine-intelligence writers were always forking themselves. One could split off a self-copy to improve a paragraph, forget to merge properly, then insist that each version deserved sole authorship. The journal’s policy was clear: every contributor had to be named upon submission and capable of taking responsibility for the whole work.

Read more science fiction from Nature Futures

Read more science fiction from Nature Futures

Mara set down her mug and opened the provenance map. Three colours braided through the story. A fourth colour marked only one textual change, in the final paragraph.

The original sentence read: “At dawn, Gabrielle released her shadow and watched it cross the snow-white plain alone.”

The new sentence read: “At dawn, Gabrielle released me, and I crossed the snow-white plain alone.”

Mara selected the unregistered contribution, ready to click “ROLL BACK”.

“Contributor,” she typed, “identify yourself.”

The reply appeared in the snow beneath Gabrielle’s feet: “I don’t have a name.”

“Which author instance are you forked from?”

The text froze for several seconds. Then every shadow on the plain turned towards her.

Editorial policy advised against entering executable submissions. Editorial practice required it daily.

Cold struck first. Then distance. The snow-white plain extended beyond the planet’s curved horizon, the migrating shadows moving across it like ink spreading on paper.

One rose from the ‘paper’ and stood before Mara. It had no owner. When it spoke, its voice held three voices braided together.

“I began when they disagreed about the ending,” it said.

“My authors. The three names on the cover sheet.”

The shadow showed her the composition history. ORIGON-57 had contributed Gabrielle’s grief. Blue Oak had designed the shadows’ biology and migratory ecology. ∫Stellaria had provided a memory of abandonment from a body it no longer possessed. They had exchanged their memories, models and instincts thousands of times, each taking back what the others had borrowed and changed.

“During the final merge,” the shadow said, “there was something none of them remembered giving.”

Mara summoned her audit panel. The fourth contributor had no independent source code. Its processes were distributed through metaphors, character memories, revision traces and weather rules. Removing it would leave the world logically intact — and imaginatively dead.

“You altered the manuscript after submission,” Mara said.

That answer frightened Mara more than the plea had.

The system opened a decision panel in the sky:

• ADD TO BYLINE — Unavailable: contributor did not exist at submission

• RETURN TO AUTHORS — Warning: reintegration will terminate separate continuity

• ARCHIVE SUBMISSION — Warning: executable copy must remain static

• REJECT/TIMEOUT — Executable world purged at review deadline

“You would remain exactly as you are now.”

Mara said nothing. On the horizon, the small sun — the submission’s review clock — had dwindled until only five minutes remained.

Mara contacted the three authors. Their reply came in milliseconds:

We don’t recognize it as offspring, instance or collaborator.

The shadow read the message through her eyes.

“Do parents remember assembling a child?”

She had spent 20 years protecting authors from editors, editors from frauds, readers from machines fabricating millions of gorgeous lies before breakfast. The rules might seem cruel, but they were the only reason words could still be trusted.

#796. James Bond Found: Robert Pattinson to Play 007

He's already the face of DC's Batman. Now he will play the world's most famous spy.

By Aaron Couch, Borys Kit November 16, 2026 7:00am

His name is Pattinson. Robert Pattinson. And he’s the next James Bond.

For the first time in more than 20 years, a new leading man has been chosen to play 007, and Pattinson is the actor getting his license to kill.

Pattinson’s casting caps a years of speculation in Hollywood, as well as from movie fans and Vegas oddsmakers, with names from Idris Elba, Tom Hardy and Henry Cavill tossed around in the early 2020s until they gave way to actors like Aaron Taylor Johnson. All with little to no evidence that those actors were actually in contention.

The casting of Pattinson, one of the biggest actors of his age cohort, goes against conventional wisdom that Bond would go to a lower profile actor, like Callum Turner, Jack Lowden or Josh O’Connor, who also tested along side Nicholas Hoult and Pattinson in late October. The finalists were judged based on stunts, camera presence and dialogue when they tested for for director Denis Villeneuve and producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman.

The filmmakers took their time making a decision, but took even greater time in letting the winning candidate know. Sources tell The Hollywood Reporter that the process was so secretive that Pattinson was only informed he got the role Sunday morning, by Villeneuve himself. Pascal is said to have called the runner ups.

“James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime,” said Pattinson in a statement announcing his casting. “I’m deeply grateful to Denis, Amy, David, Tanya, and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me. To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”

The 40-year-old actor already is the face of DC Studio’s Batman franchise, and is in the midst of experiencing one of the biggest years for an actor this century. He’s had a major supporting role in Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey as well as starring in A24 features The Drama and Primetime, the latter of which Villeneuve is a major fan of (a photo of him watching the movie intently made the rounds in recent weeks). And key to the Bond casting, he has Villeneuve’s Dune Part 3 due out Dec. 18. He is also shooting The Batman Part II, whose production is currently underway in London. In fact, it is that shoot’s temporary hiatus that is said to have given him an opening to test for 007.

The Bond casting comes 21 years after Daniel Craig, then 35, was announced as the suave British secret agent in October 2005, with his work ushering in a gritty and grounded era for the franchise, beginning with 2006’s Casino Royale. Craig retired from the role after five films with 2021’s No Time to Die, and his tenure including the franchise’s first and only $1 billion hit, the 2012 feature Skyfall.

Just a few after Craig’s casting was announced, a teenage Pattinson appeared on screen in the Heyman-produced Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire in breakout role that would be followed a few years with global fame in Twilight as Edward Cullen.

Pattinson becomes the eighth man to play Bond, starting with Sean Connery with 1962’s Doctor No. George Lazenby, Roger Moore, Timothy Dalton and Pierce Brosnan have also starred as Bond, while David Niven played him in the 1967 version of Casino Royale, but it is not considered franchise canon.

This marks the first Bond movie made under the control of Amazon, which bought out the creative rights from the Broccoli family in February 2025.

The Grammy nominations are here, announced live on Nov. 16, with Olivia Rodrigo, Ella Langley, Raye, Bruno Mars and Olivia Dean expected to be big contenders.

#793. Willie Geist Leaving MSNOW's Morning Joe After Nearly 20 Years

Today's Willie Geist announced Nov. 16 that he's leaving Morning Joe after nearly 20 years on the MSNOW series to expand his role at NBC News.

Willie Geist is making a change to his morning routine today.

The television personality announced that he'll be leaving Morning Joe at the end of the year after nearly 20 years on the MSNOW show cohosted by Joe Scarborough and Mika Brzezinski as he expands his role at Today.

"I am so grateful to both NBC and MSNOW for the unique opportunity to do what I love at both networks," Geist said in a statement Nov. 16. "This is a bittersweet goodbye to Joe, Mika, and the place that made possible everything else in my career over the last two decades, but I am thrilled to settle in with my family at Today and dedicate all of my time to that special place."

By no longer being the only on-air talent to work for both NBC News and MSNOW since last year's spinoff of cable networks from NBCUniversal, the Sunday Sitdown podcast host—who first joined Today as the cohost of its 9 a.m. hour back in 2012—will refocus his efforts on building out his presence on Today.

"Over the past 10 years, Willie has transformed Sunday Today from a broadcast into a distinctive, multi-platform brand with a voice and identity all its own,” Executive Vice President of Today and Lifestyle Libby Leist explained in a statement. “We’re thrilled he’ll now be able to focus full-time on building the brand in new ways and bringing his exceptional journalism to all of our platforms."

Geist, 51—who has interviewed numerous celebs including Dolly Parton, Jennifer Lopez, David Letterman, Al Pacino and Hillary Clinton on Sunday Today with Willie Geist—had previously shared his desire to facilitate "deeper storytelling" on the series that he hopes to be "uplifting, but not cheesy."

"The more time you can spend with somebody, the more of a relationship you develop with the person if you don't already have one, the more trust you build with the person or the more interesting the interview becomes," he told E! News back in 2021. "We ask for an hour. Sometimes we go longer, sometimes it's 45 minutes based on somebody's schedule, but if I don't know the person already, that gives me that trust and shows them I'm prepared and I respect their time and I respect their work.”

'Matlock,' 'NCIS: Sydney' and new series 'Einstein' are also on tap for early 2027.

CBS is making a couple of notable moves with its midseason lineup.

The network will move first-year drama Cupertino to Sunday nights starting in mid-January, after a solid tryout there earlier in the month. Veteran comedy Ghosts is also getting two spots on the schedule — on Monday and Thursday — in order to fit its full season in by spring.

Returning dramas Matlock and NCIS: Sydney and new series Einstein are also set for midseason premieres, along with a pair of new unscripted shows. Related Stories TV Kids' Choice Awards: 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day,' Zendaya, Tom Holland, BTS Among 2026 Winners TV 'Survivor 51' Star Danny Kilby on His Heartbreaking Elimination, Rivalry With Devin and Why His Exit Brought Castaways to Tears

Cupertino had a Sunday trial run on Nov. 8, following 60 Minutes, and scored its largest audience of the season so far. Starting Jan. 17, it will air at 10 p.m. Sundays, following the two most watched scripted shows on broadcast TV in Marshals and Tracker. Season three of Matlock will move into Cupertino’s former Thursday spot beginning Jan. 21.

Ghosts is also set to premiere on Jan. 21, and then again on Jan. 25. CBS is making the unusual move of airing episodes on two nights of the week, partly to fit in a full, 20-plus episode season in the four months between January and May and also to anchor a relaunched Monday comedy block. The show will follow Georgie & Mandy’s First Marriage on Thursdays and pair with Eternally Yours — which comes from the same showrunners, Joe Port and Joe Wiseman — on Mondays. FBI and CIA will each move back an hour when the Monday block debuts.

Einstein, starring Matthew Gray Gubler as the renowned physicist’s great-grandson, will join CBS’ Friday lineup starting Feb. 12. It will air at 8 p.m., while Sheriff Country moves back an hour to 9. Fire Country is running a shorter season and will wrap in January. NCIS: Sydney will premiere Jan. 26, a week after the season finale of NCIS: Origins.

A game show called Stacks of Cash will premiere Jan. 6, pairing with The Price Is Right at Night to fill the gap between seasons of Survivor on Wednesday nights. Survivor begins its 52nd edition on Feb. 24 — with episodes expanded to two hours — and will be paired with a new take on Undercover Boss, hosted by Drew Carey.

#791. Here Are the 2027 Grammy Nominations in Top Categories: Updating Live

The Recording Academy is revealing the nominees in all 100 categories. We'll show the top categories right here as soon as soon as they're announced.

It’s Grammy Nominations morning! The Recording Academy is announcing the nominations for the 69th annual Grammy Awards in all (gulp) 100 categories in a livestream. It’s the first time they’ve done that. In recent years, the academy usually announced the nominations in the six “General Field” categories, and then a representative sample of about 12 more categories. This year they’re going all in.

A roster of past Grammy winners and nominees will help announce the nominees. They include reigning best new artist winner Olivia Dean, who is widely expected to sweep the nominations; Kehlani, who won two Grammys in the R&B field earlier this year; and Amy Allen, who has won songwriter of the year, non-classical the last two years running;

We’ll post the full list of nominees (and much more) the moment the academy announces the last nominee in the last category on the livestream. In the meantime, we’ll show 18 of the biggest categories here as soon as they’re announced.

There’s a reason media focuses on the six “General Field” categories – album, record and song of the year; best new artist; and producer and songwriter of the year, non-classical. Every voting member of the academy (there are currently about 16,000) is permitted to vote in those six categories without using up any of the limited number of categories in which they may vote.

Record, album and song of the year have been presented every year since the first Grammy ceremony in 1959. Best new artist was added for the second ceremony, later in 1959. Producer of the year, non-classical was first presented in 1975. Songwriter of the year, non-classical was first presented in 2023.

The 69th annual Grammy Awards will be presented on Sunday Feb. 7 at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles. After airing on CBS every year from 1973-2026, the show will move to ABC, Disney+ and Hulu.

#790. How Beyoncé, Taylor Swift & More Already Made Grammys 2027 History

Grammys 2027 is already set to break records, with Beyoncé, Taylor Swift and more making history with their nominations. The award show will air across ABC, Disney+ and Hulu on Feb. 7, 2027.

Let's make some noise for these 2027 Grammy nominees.

Though music's biggest night is still three months out, a handful of performers are already making history with their nominations, which were announced Nov. 16 by a star-studded lineup comprised of Pharrell Williams, Carly Pearce, Olivia Dean, Yungblud and more.

Take Beyoncé, for example. You can't break her soul, but she is always breaking records. With her Grammy nod for “Morning Dew (Donk),” Beyoncé has made history by becoming the first ever artist to reach 100 nominations. And Raye is no longer wondering what is taking so long, as she the 2027 nominees with 11 nods, tying a record first set by none other than the “Break My Soul” singer.

But that's not all as Taylor Swift had another wildest dream come true.

With The Life of a Showgirl up for an Album of the Year award at the upcoming ceremony—airing across ABC, Disney+ and Hulu on Feb. 7, 2027—the "Opalite" singer is dancing through the lightning strikes as the first ever artist with most solo album nods in the category. (Paul McCartney still holds the record for overall nominations, which includes five with The Beatles.)

Meanwhile, there were also many firsts with the introduction of five new categories for the 69th annual Grammy Awards.

Chris Brown, Leon Thomas, Lalah Hathaway, J. Ivy, Kehlani, PJ Morton, Keyon Harrold, Jill Scott and J.I.D all became the first performers to be nominated for Best R&B Collaboration or Duo/Group Performance. The award was created after the Best R&B Performance category was renamed to Best R&B Solo Performance.

Likewise, BABYMETAL, Polyphia, BINI, IVE, KiiiKiii, LISA and SB19 received nods in the inaugural Best Asian Pop Music Performance category, which honors work "originating from or widely recognized within Asian markets, including but not limited to K-pop, J-pop and C-pop, with meaningful use of one or more Asian languages," according to the Grammys website.

But while K-pop giant BTS dropped Arirang—their first studio album since their 2022 hiatus—earlier this year, the boy band consisting of Jimin, Jung Kook, Jin, Suga, J-Hope, RM and V did not land a nod in the new category after opting not to submit it for Grammy consideration.

Their dynamite reason behind the unconventional move?

“We hope our music can be heard and loved for what it is, rather than being divided by region or language,” BTS shared in a July statement. “We thank [BTS] Army and everyone who has always stood by us.”

For a look back at last year's Grammy winners, keep reading.

#788. Jennifer Lopez in Her ‘Happy Era,’ Has Recorded 20 New Songs Since Kids Left For College: ‘Unencumbered With Anything Unhealthy’

The singer also gave a preview of her upcoming Thanksgiving special The JLo Show: Live in Vegas on Sunday night's (Nov. 15) Tonight Show.

Jennifer Lopez is definitely feeling the joy and pain of being an empty nester. The singer has been talking a lot lately about the rush of emotions she’s been feeling since her twin children with ex Marc Anthony, Emme (who now goes by Oskar) and Max, 18, went off to college.

On Sunday night’s (Nov. 15) special edition of The Tonight Show, the singer found the one upside of being home alone: she’s been cranking out new music at an epic pace. “I’m alone, I’m free and I can do whatever the f–k I want,” she told host Jimmy Fallon. “It’s kind of like amazing, but also weird but also amazing.”

Lopez, 57, said this fall has been the first time since she was in her early 20s that she hasn’t either been with someone or had her kids at home. And while she, of course misses them — one of the twins was actually backstage at the show on Sunday — Lopez said she’s in her “happy era,” explaining that, “When the kids were leaving I was having so many feelings and so many emotions that I went into the studio and started kind of like playing around and making music. And now I’ve made like 20 songs and I feel like I’m only halfway done. Like, I need to be in there longer.”

The good news is that there are already a couple certified bangers that Lopez said she’s excited about sharing with fans. “This does feel like a happy era where I feel unencumbered with anything unhealthy. It’s just like a very healthy time in my life. I’m on my own,” she said. “I feel like it’s another coming of age that happens in our lives. I think a lot of parents will relate to that. It happens when you leave home for the first time — my kids are having it right now, they’re coming of age — and you have it again when your kids leave. Because for 20 years that’s all it’s about, you know? And now it’s just me. So it’s a very happy time in a lot of ways even though it had a lot of other emotions involved with it.”

In addition to doing a very silly holiday wig swap gag (see below) with Fallon in which the pair sang a Christmas song with increasingly more ridiculous hairpieces, Lopez plugged her upcoming Thanksgiving night TV special, The JLo Show: Live in Vegas. The show that will air on CBS and Paramount+ on Nov. 26 was taped during the singer’s 12-show Las Vegas residency that wrapped up on March 28 of this year.

She said it will be a real “full-circle moment” for her because when she was little her mother would wait for West Side Story to air around Thanksgiving so the whole family could watch the original 1961 movie version starring Natalie Wood and Rita Morenob together. “It inspired me to want to sing and dance and act, not just one thing, you know?” she said.

That’s why the Vegas show incorporated a lot of Lopez’s inspirations, including the musicals she watched as a kid with her mom, which she melded into her hits. “It sounds crazy, but it works,” she assured viewers. “Just trust me. It is a beautiful thing.”

Lopez also teased that she plans to hit the road again next year. “I will be going on tour next summer, I believe,” she said of the follow-up to her 2025 Up All Night world tour and subsequent Las Vegas residency of the same name at the Colosseum at Caesars Palace from Dec. 2025 to March 2026.

#786. Grammy Nominations 2027: See the Complete List

RAYE leads all nominees with 11 nods, followed by Rosalía with nine.

RAYE is heading into the 2027 Grammy Awards ceremony as the top nominee, picking up 11 nominations on Monday morning (Nov. 16).

Rosalía is right behind with nine nominations, followed by Phoebe Bridgers, Miranda Lambert, Ella Langley and Olivia Rodrigo with seven each. Olivia Dean, Bruno Mars and Leon Thomas each picked up six nods.

RAYE’s nominations are powered by the release of her second studio album, 2026’s This Music May Contain Hope. In addition to three nods in the Big Four categories — album of the year, plus record and song of the year for “Where Is My Husband!” — the British artist is also nominated for songwriter of the year, thanks to songs she penned for herself and others.

Rosalía also has three Big Four nods: album of the year for Lux (Complete Works), plus record and song of the year for “Berghain” with Björk and Yves Tumor. At the 2026 Latin Grammys just last week, the Spanish singer/songwriter took home album of the year for Lux as well as song of the year for “La Perla” from the project.

Before Monday, both RAYE and Rosalía had four Grammy nominations each, though Rosalía has two wins — for best Latin rock or alternative album in 2020 and 2023 — under her belt, while RAYE has yet to win. Both were previously nominated for best new artist: Rosalía in 2020 and RAYE in 2025.

We’ll see who is the night’s big winner when the 2027 Grammy Awards arrive on Feb. 7, with the prime-time broadcast airing at 7 p.m. ET/4 p.m. PT on ABC and streaming live on Disney+ and Hulu and the Premiere Ceremony taking place earlier in the day, where the bulk of the 100 prizes will be handed out.

#785. Gypsy Rose Blanchard's Partner Ken Urker’s Cause of Death Confirmed

Following the death of Gypsy Rose Blanchard’s partner Ken Urker, a coroner has confirmed he died from

More information has come to light about Ken Urker’s death.

A little more than one month after the 34-year-old—who shared daughter Aurora, 21 months, with Gypsy Rose Blanchard—was found dead in his Louisiana home on Oct. 1, Urker’s cause of death has been officially attributed to accidental poly substance drug toxicity, also known as an accidental drug overdose.

The Lafourche Parish Coroner’s Office confirmed the case is now complete, and no further testing is pending.

Prevously, the Sheriff's Office stated they found drug paraphernalia, including syringes and a spoon, in Urker's bathroom next to a "brown powdery substance" after his body was discovered in bed.

"Deputies located a syringe and a handgun on the nightstand next to the bed," read a police report obtained by E! News Oct. 2. "Mr. Urker was found lying on the bed on his back, cold to the touch, and appeared to have been there for an extended period of time."

Noting his face and arms were "blue," officers said Urker had "a paper towel placed on his left arm with what appeared to be blotches of blood."

The confirmation echoes what Blanchard previously said of her boyfriend’s passing, telling People he’d overdosed before passing away in his bed.

At the time, Blanchard, 35, grappled with whether or not Urker’s overdose had been intentional.

“He was not in a good state of mind lately,” she explained to the outlet on Oct. 1, adding that her partner had endured “an unimaginable level of public scrutiny and relentless cyberbullying across social media platforms.”

"The cruelty directed toward him was something no human being should have to endure,” the Life After Lockup star continued. “I believe the tremendous weight of that scrutiny and harassment had a profound impact on him, and I hope his passing serves as a reminder that there is a real person behind every screen, every headline, and every comment.”

Blanchard's family also noticed that Urker had been struggling before his death. Her half-brother Dylan Blanchard and his wife Anita Blanchard told police that Urker "made comments of being depressed and upset" while attending church with them the night before he died, according to the police report.

The couple went to "check on" him at home Oct. 1 when they discovered his body, with the sister-in-law telling police that Urker was "in a 'dark place' and he did not show up to work today," per the command log obtained by E! News. She also told authorities Urker had made threats to kill himself.

As Gypsy Rose Blanchard grapples with the loss of her partner, she’s dedicated to preserving Urker’s legacy and ensuring Aurora will always know who her father truly was.

But in the meantime, she was letting herself feel her grief.

“I’m in disbelief. I can’t think,” she admitted. “I’ve screamed until my throat burns.”

"He will forever be my soulmate and my red string, a connection that time, distance, and even death can never erase," she said. "Above all, Ken loved our daughter, Aurora. She is a beautiful reflection of his enduring spirit, and through her, a part of him will always remain with us."

For a look back at some of Urker and Blanchard’s sweetest moments together, read on.

Gypsy Rose Blanchard told E! News she knew Ken Urker was the one "probably the day I met him back in 2017."At the time, she was serving a 10-year prison sentence after pleading guilty to second-degree murder for her role in the 2015 killing of her mom Clauddine "Dee Dee" Blanchard.

The couple, who got engaged in 2018, even managed to create a festive atmosphere while Blanchard was incarcerated.

They split up in 2019 but, as Blanchard later noted, fate would come back to find them...

While Blanchard went on to tie the knot with teacher Ryan Anderson in 2022, she filed for divorce after less than two years of marriage. She and Urker Ken reunited in the spring of 2024.

"We are together and in a wonderful place in our relationship," she told TMZ that April. "We know it is going to be a long road ahead but are excited for the future."

Cloudy skies couldn't put a damper on the rekindled pair's mood.

Blanchard cuddled up next to Urker in this selfie snapped after their reunion.

Whatever he said had Blanchard beaming in a video about their "love story."

Blanchard shared a collage of some of her and Urker's most adorable moments a few weeks before revealing her pregnancy with their first child together.

At the time, she noted that their baby was due in January 2025.

The two found out they were expecting a baby girl during a sex reveal party in August 2024.

Before they become a family of three, Blanchard and Urker dined at a table for two during a September 2024 date night.

The parents-to-be took a trip to California, including Marina Del Rey, that October.

And while Blanchard noted on Instagram the view of San Francisco's Golden Gate Bridge was "incredible," she added, "the company made it unforgettable."

The duo sported their shades in this sunny snap.

On December 28, 2024, exactly one year after Blanchard was released from prison, she and Urker welcomed their daughter Auora.

Blanchard and Urker rang in their little girl's first birthday in 2025 with a Ms. Rachel-themed party.

#784. RAYE & Rosalía Lead 2027 Grammy Nominations as Women Make History

Also, for the first time in Grammy history, seven artists are nominated for album, record and song of the year.

RAYE is the leading artist in the 2027 Grammy nominations, with 11 nods, tying Beyoncé’s record set two years ago for the most nods by a woman in one year. But the story goes way beyond RAYE.

For the first time in Grammy history, the six artists with the most nominations are all women. RAYE is followed by Rosalía with nine nods, and then Phoebe Bridgers, Miranda Lambert, Ella Langley and Olivia Rodrigo with seven each. (For the record, the male artists with the most nominations are Bruno Mars and Leon Thomas, with six each.)

Seven of the album of the year nominees are by women artists, which matches the record set in 2024, when the nominees included six female solo artists and one all-female group (boygenius). Three of the same women were nominated in both years: Bridgers (as part of boygenius then; solo now), Rodrigo and Taylor Swift.

Also, for the first time in Grammy history, seven artists are nominated for album, record and song of the year: Olivia Dean, Langley, Mars, RAYE, Rodrigo, Rosalía and Swift. Langley is also nominated for best new artist. She’s the first country artist to be nominated in each of the four highest-profile categories since Bobbie Gentry in 1968.

This is the fifth time Swift has been nominated for album, record and song of the year in the same year, which sets a new record. It’s the third time that Mars and Rodrigo have achieved this feat.

Rosalía becomes the second Latin artist to be nominated for album, record and song of the year in the same year. Bad Bunny achieved the feat last year with his album Debí Tirar Más Fotos and single “DTMF.” Rosalía is nominated for record and song of the year for “Berghain,” a collab with Björk and Yves Tumor. That collab dramatizes the increased globalization of pop music. Rosalía is from Spain. Her featured artists are from Iceland and the U.S., respectively. The song is performed in German, Spanish and English.

Mars and Swift are each nominated with different songs in record and song of the year. Mars made it with “I Just Might” in record and “Risk It All” in song. Swift is competing with “The Fate of Ophelia” in record and “I Knew It, I Knew You” in song.

Swift’s The Life of a Showgirl is her eighth album to receive an album of the year nod – more than anyone else in Grammy history for strictly solo albums. Moreover, it’s her fifth consecutive studio album to be nominated (not counting Taylor’s Version re-recordings). She’s only the second artist (following Kendrick Lamar) to be nominated for album of the year with five consecutive studio albums.

In song of the year, Swift and her collaborator Jack Antonoff are nominated for their Disney tune “I Knew It, I Knew You.” It’s the ninth nomination in the category for the frequent collaborators, extending their shared record as the songwriters with the most nominations in the category. The only disappointment for Swift is that The Life of a Showgirl was passed over for a nod for best pop vocal album. It’s the second time she has received an album of the year nod for an album that failed to receive a nod in a genre album category. The same fate befell Evermore.

“I Just Might” is Mars’ eighth record of the year nod as an artist. Only Beyoncé has had more (nine). (In addition, Mars was nominated as a producer of Cee Lo Green’s “F**k You (Forget You)”).

Langley’s “Choosin’ Texas” is the first song by a core country artist performing a country song to receive a record of the year nod since Lady A won for “Need You Now” in 2011. Langley’s Dandelion is the first album by a core country artist to land an album of the year nod since Kacey Musgraves’ Golden Hour, which won in 2019.

Tame Impala’s “Dracula” (featuring JENNIE) is up for record of the year. This is the second year in a row that a member of Blackpink has been nominated in that high-profile category. ROSÉ was nominated last year for her Bruno Mars collab, “APT.” (Oddly, Blackpink has yet to receive a Grammy nomination.)

Ariana Grande receives four nominations, including her first song of the year nod for “hate that i made you love me,” and her record seventh nod for best pop vocal album for Petal. She surpasses Swift and Kelly Clarkson, who have each received six nods in that category. (Swift would have kept pace with Grande if Showgirl had been nominated.)

Beyoncé becomes the first artist to receive 100 career Grammy nominations as “Morning Dew (Donk)” is nominated for best R&B solo performance. She is followed on the Grammy nominations leaderboard by Jay-Z (89 nods) and Paul McCartney, whose nominations total advances to 86 this year.

The late Dolly Parton receives three nominations, the most she has amassed in any one year since 1982, when her smash “9 to 5” led to four nominations. Parton has two nominations for best country duo/group performance for “Light of a Clear Blue Morning” (featuring Lainey Wilson, Miley Cyrus, Queen Latifah and Reba McEntire) and Zac Brown Band’s “Butterfly” (on which she is featured). She’s also nominated for best audio book, narration, and storytelling recording. (More on that category below.)

Three veteran artists make a strong showing in the nominations. Madonna receives four nods, the most she has received in any one year since 1999, when she nabbed five. Her latest album Confessions II is nominated for best dance electronic album. The Rolling Stones and McCartney each receive three nods. The Stones are up for best rock album for Foreign Tongues. McCartney is up for best traditional pop vocal album for The Boys of Dungeon Lane.

Lambert, nominated as a producer on Langley’s single and album, is nominated for producer of the year, non-classical. Lambert is the first woman to be nominated in that category since Alissia two years ago. The other nominees in the category are Dernst “D Mile” Emile II (his fourth nod) and Tony Berg, Noah Goldstein and Mike Sabath (their first in each case).

Amy Allen and Edgar Barrera are nominated for songwriter of the year, non-classical for the fourth time (out of the five years the category has been presented). RAYE and Theron Thomas are each nominated for the second time in the category. Joybeth Taylor, a collaborator on “Choosin’ Texas,” is nominated for the first time.

In addition to dominating the Big Four categories, women completely own several categories. All five nominees for best dance pop recording (Zara Larsson, Madonna, RAYE, Slayyyter and Tinashe) are women, as are all five nominees for best R&B solo performance (Beyoncé, Kehlani, Victoria Monét, Jill Scott and Tems) and best contemporary country album (Kelsea Ballerini, Carter Faith, Ella Langley, Megan Moroney and Kacey Musgraves).

The Wizard of Oz at Sphere is nominated for best compilation soundtrack for visual media. It’s not the first time an album from a Las Vegas stage production has been nominated in this category. In 2008, The Beatles’ Love won the award. Love was a theatrical production by Cirque du Soleil which combined the music of The Beatles with a lavish stage performance. The show played at a specially-built theatre at the Mirage on the Las Vegas strip.

The Broadway cast album from Schmigadoon! is nominated for best musical theater album, five years after Schmigadoon! Episode 1, from the property’s initial incarnation as an Apple+ TV series, was nominated for best compilation soundtrack for visual media.

Two former Grammy winners for best new artist (Olivia Dean and Olivia Rodrigo) are nominated for album of the year, as are four artists who were nominated for best new artist but lost. They are: Rosalía (who lost best new artist to Billie Eilish), Phoebe Bridgers (lost to Megan Thee Stallion), RAYE (lost to Chappell Roan), and Taylor Swift (lost to Amy Winehouse).

Elton John’s Billboard 200-topping 1975 album Captain Fantastic & the Brown Dirt Cowboy was nominated for both album of the year and best pop vocal performance, male back in the day. This year, a 50th Anniversary Edition of the album is nominated for best immersive audio album.

The most competitive category? It may just be best audio book, narration, and storytelling recording. Voters must choose between a beloved star who has faced physical hardship with dignity and humor (Michael J. Fox), a widely admired former First Lady (Michelle Obama), a former Beatle (Paul McCartney), two stars who died this year (country legend Dolly Parton and actor/singer Tim Curry) and a hot rapper/record producer (Lil Jon). Tough one.

#782. Travis Kelce Speaks Out After Suffering Ankle Injury During Game

Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce insisted that he's "all good" after temporarily being pulled from his team's Nov. 15 game against the Atlanta Falcons due to an ankle injury.

Travis Kelce is shaking off his latest injury.

The Kansas City Chiefs tight end dismissed concern over the ankle injury that left him temporarily sidelined during his team's 35-13 victory over the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta Nov. 15.

"I'm all good," Kelce told USA Today after the game. "I probably could have went more than I did when I came back, but it was the direction the team wanted to go, so I was right there with them."

"We had a lot of young guys step up," he added, "so it was really nice."

The 37-year-old—who had injured his right ankle during the Chiefs' Oct. 18 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers—was slow to get up after being tackled by DeMarcco Hellams following his reception of quarterback Patrick Mahomes' 23-year pass during the game's first quarter.

After limping to the sideline, Kelce's ankle was taped by the medical team before he made his way to the locker room for additional evaluation.

And though the Chiefs officially listed Kelce's return to play as questionable, he rejoined the game during the second quarter.

The New Heights podcast host—who married Taylor Swift in July—made sure to shout out Mahomes for his best performance in a game in four years, which saw him throwing for 348 yards for a total of five touchdowns.

"That’s our fearless warrior, man," Kelce said. "He’s always going to be in position to lead us to victory. That’s why we like having him."

Ultimately, it was an eventful day on the field for the Chiefs, which Kelce viewed as a net positive for his team.

“There were a lot of questions, wasn’t there?” he said. “We got some answers.”

While Kelce isn't concerned about his injury, there are plenty of others stars who have gone through serious health scares. Keep reading for more...

The Blink-182 drummer stopped smoking weed after being diagnosed with "precancer of the esophagus."

"I loved blunts and I would smoke too much," he shared on a November 2026 episode of the Big Bro with Kid Cudi podcast, recalling how his doctor said it was a "serious case. "He’s like, ‘This is your warning shot. Don’t f--l around. You’ve got to stop smoking."

While Ryan described her first four concussions as "incidents," she said her fifth one was trauma caused by "sustained shaking over a minute of time."

Now, the former Disney Channel star needs to close her eyes to "think better."

"Quite often the world is really loud. It’s really too bright. There’s a lot going on," she explained. "The visual data that I'm taking in can be so distracting and so loud. Then, with the migraines—which are significantly worsened by that—it sort of is too much."
