Emilia Clarke filmed battle scenes for Game of Thrones, but in 2019, she published an essay in The New Yorker titled "A Battle for My Life."Having a bad headache at the gym, "I reached the toilet, sank to my knees, and proceeded to be violently, voluminously ill," the actress wrote. "Meanwhile, the pain—shooting, stabbing, constricting pain—was getting worse. At some level, I knew what was happening: my brain was damaged."She was taken to the hospital for a brain scan."The diagnosis was quick and ominous: a subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), a life-threatening type of stroke, caused by bleeding into the space surrounding the brain," the Emmy nominee added. "I’d had an aneurysm, an arterial rupture."Emilia had immediate surgery to seal the aneurysm, calling the pain "unbearable." While she was recovering, she continued, she experienced aphasia and was "muttering nonsense."A week later, "the aphasia passed," Emilia added, and she left the hospital a month after being admitted. At a 2013 brain scan, she learned a growth "doubled in size" and that she needed surgery again."When they woke me, I was screaming in pain," she wrote. "The procedure had failed. I had a massive bleed and the doctors made it plain that my chances of surviving were precarious if they didn’t operate again. This time they needed to access my brain in the old-fashioned way—through my skull."Thankfully, Emilia shared, she's now "at a hundred per cent."

Snoop Dogg's daughter Cori Broadus is grateful for her family.Because after she suffered a "severe stroke" in January 2024, her loved ones rushed to be by her side."I texted them that I just had a stroke and sent them a picture," she told E! News correspondent Will Marfuggi in December 2024. "Everybody just came to my rescue."Because of other medical concerns, Cori ended up staying in the hospital longer than she initially expected."I could have went home after my stroke, but my lupus wasn't doing so well," the Snoop's Fatherhood: Cori and Wayne's Story star continued. "My kidneys were failing. It was a lot going on."Today, Cori is on the mend."I'm doing great," she added. "I just had a little bit of motor skills that I had to work back on. But other than that, I was fine."

Shailene Woodley’s early 20s were not an easy time health-wise.“It got to the point where I was losing my hearing. I couldn’t walk for longer than five minutes at a time without having to lay down for hours, and hours and sleep. Everything I ate hurt my stomach,” the actress said on a September 2024 episode of the SHE MD Podcast. “It was this conflation of issues and diagnoses and different doctors telling me different things.”So Shailene—who chose to keep the exact condition private—set out to find answers. “I come from a very holistic background and study herbalism,” she added. “So I was very keen on, ‘I’m going to work with real MDs, [and] I’m also going to work with independent kind of healers.’ Just trying to search for some sense of comfort in my own skin.”It was a long journey—one that lasted for 10 years.“Throughout that decade, a lot of other things came from feeling so much discomfort physically,” the Big Little Lies star noted, “which was, ‘My gosh, if everything I eat hurts my stomach, I’m now suddenly afraid of food.’ And then going into the kind of mental f--ckery that can happen with that of body dysmorphia and confusion about identity and feeling safe in my own capsule, in my own skin, what that meant, and what that should be.”After tending to both her physical and mental health, Shailene is feeling much better.“It was a journey that ultimately physically resolved itself, and I am very healthy,” she shared. “I’m so happy to be able to say that."

#781. Snubs & Surprises In the 2027 Grammy Nominations

Grammy voters always have a few surprises up their sleeves.

We all knew that the Olivias (Dean and Rodrigo) were going to get a lot of love from Grammy voters this year. And sure enough, when nominations for the 69th annual Grammy Awards were announced bright and early on Monday (Nov. 16), they both did. So did such other expected names as Taylor Swift, Bruno Mars and Rosalía.

And it’s hardly a surprise that women dominated the nominations, though the degree of that dominance is impressive. For the first time in Grammy history, the six artists with the most nominations are all women. RAYE leads with 11 nods, followed by Rosalía with nine nods, and then Phoebe Bridgers, Miranda Lambert, Ella Langley and Olivia Rodrigo, with seven each.

But that doesn’t mean there were no surprises in the nominations. It’s impossible to have 100 categories without having at least a few outcomes that don’t land as expected. This year, nearly 16,000 voting members of the Recording Academy were eligible to vote. That includes more than 2,300 new voting members who joined as part of the 2026 new member class.

Final-round voting will take place from Dec. 10 to Jan. 7. The 69th annual Grammy Awards will air on Sunday, Feb. 7, at a new time – 7 p.m. ET/ 4 p.m. PT. The move was designed to let Grammy watchers on the East Coast watch the full show without having to stay up to midnight.

Here are some of the most notable snubs and surprises from the 69th annual Grammy nominations list.

Many expected Kahan to be nominated for album, record and song of the year, but he was completely overlooked in all three of those marquee categories. His only nod was for The Great Divide: The Last of the Bugs (the deluxe edition of his Billboard 200-topping album), which is nominated for best contemporary folk album. Whatever the reasons, after a few years of being one of the top music artists in America, Kahan has received a grand total of three Grammy nods. He might do well to remind himself of this truth, nicely articulated by a talented troubadour: “California’s so much more than some awards show.”

Antonoff received three nods – album of the year for Phoebe Bridgers’ Lost Weekend and song of the year and best song written for visual media for “I Knew It, I Knew You,” his collab with Taylor Swift. But he was passed over for a nod for producer of the year, non-classical for the third year in a row.

The jazz pianist, composer and bandleader died in February 2021, but he just keeps piling up Grammy nominations. He received two more this year – best jazz instrumental album for Forever Yours: The Farewell Performance (Live) and best arrangement, instrumental or a cappella for “Overjoyed (Live).” Corea has won six of his 29 Grammys since he died.

Lefty had one of the year’s biggest pop/country crossover hits with “Boston,” but was bypassed in the CMA Awards nominations and now is also omitted from the Grammy nominations. The accusations of plagiarism that tarnished her breakthrough moment likely kept voters from supporting her.

Some speculated that the talented brother and sister might both receive best new artist nominations in the same year, which would have been a Grammy Awards first. Neither did.

These three artists were in the conversation for best new artist, but few expected them to actually make it. But all three did make it. The Womack Sisters are the first sister act to be nominated since Chloe x Halle (Bailey) eight years ago. Zeimani, Zekkujcha, and Zekuumba Womack are daughters of musicians Linda and Cecil Womack, members of the R&B duo Womack & Womack, and nieces of singer Bobby Womack and granddaughters of singer Sam Cooke.

Both artists were touted as best new artist hopefuls; both fell short. Fender had a long-running Hot 100 hit with “Rein Me In,” but voters may have figured anybody could have a Hot 100 hit at this point if they teamed up with the red-hot Olivia Dean. Role Model’s failure to receive a nod may be due to voters expecting a stronger follow-up to his irresistible late 2025 viral hit “Sally, When the Wine Runs Out.”

Summit’s sophomore album, Ctrl Escape, was blanked in the nominations. Summit’s camp had submitted the album for best dance/electronic album, and two of its tracks in other categories – “Lights Go Out” for best dance/electronic recording and “Don’t Believe It” (with Absolutely) for best dance pop recording. Summit expressed his displeasure on X, saying “the whole dance category is just music industry fueled pop stars” rather than a celebration of authentic electronic music culture. Summit (who promoted his 2024 album Comfort in Chaos with a performance and interview at the Grammy Museum in L.A.) declared he will never submit his music to the Recording Academy again unless significant changes are made to how electronic/dance music is judged.

never submitting to the grammys again unless shit changes, it’s all a fucking joke. i’m not just talking about myself either there’s zero respect for real electronic dance music & dj’s. the whole dance category is just music industry fueled pop stars

Spiro is nominated for best new artist, as widely expected, but her elegant ballad “Die on This Hill” was passed over for both record and song of the year nods. Not a shock – the record peaked at No. 19 on the Hot 100, a bit low to register in such a competitive category – but it had echoes of Adele’s breakthrough hit “Chasing Pavements,” which was nominated in both categories in 2009.

Wicked: For Good didn’t receive a single Oscar nomination earlier this year, but Grammy voters supported the project. The album is up for best compilation soundtrack for visual media, while “No Place Like Home” is up for best song written for visual media and Cynthia Erivo and Ariana Grande’s collaboration on “For Good” is nominated for best traditional pop vocal performance. Last year, the first Wicked was nominated for best compilation soundtrack, while “Defying Gravity” won a Grammy for best pop duo/group performance.

#780. Grammy Nominations 2027 Snubs & Surprises: Noah Kahan, Raye & More

The Recording Academy revealed its 2027 Grammy nominations, with Beyoncé and Raye walking away with major recognition. Noah Kahan and Harry Styles, meanwhile, were absent in major categories.

Get ready to turn up the volume on the biggest night in music.

After all, the 2027 Grammy Awards nominations were announced on Nov. 16 with a pitch-perfect lineup of presenters, including David Guetta, Kehlani, Olivia Dean and Yungblud.

Taylor Swift proved she knows what it takes to put on a show, earning five nominations for her album The Life of a Showgirl as well as her Toy Story 5 track "I Knew It, I Knew You," including Album of the Year and Song of the Year.

Meanwhile, Olivia Rodrigo is ready for a golden evening after being nominated seven times over for her album you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love in categories including Album of the Year and Song of the Year, as well as Best Rock Performance and Best Rock Song for "What's Wrong With Me?" featuring Robert Smith.

Phoebe Bridgers made a triumphant return with her third solo album Lost Boys—her first in more than six years—earning seven nods like Album of the Year and Best Alternative Music Album.

Raye, for her part, was on every nomination shortlist, but she exceeded even the most elevated expectations, earning 11 nominations, tying Beyoncé's 2025 record for the most nominations by a single female artist in a single year.

That's not to say all the most-listened-to songs or albums made the list. Although fans expected Noah Kahan to be among the contenders for Album of the Year, The Great Divide appeared to fall flat with the Recording Academy, save for one nod for Best Contemporary Folk Album.

The same goes for Harry Styles, who failed to score a single nod for his album Kiss All The Time, Disco Occasionally. Meanwhile, despite Stella Lefty's massive hit "Boston" dominating charts this year, she failed to score a Best New Artist nomination.

And while Adéla prays every single night, she won't be sitting right at the Grammys for her earworm song "Nicole Kidman"—a decision she made for herself.

"I think it's a nomination you need to earn," she told Who What Wear earlier this month of the Song of the Year category. "I have so much more work to do before I even think of that. I have my tour, and I want to start writing my next album."

But that's not to say the 22-year-old won't return to try to prove her weight in gold.

"I think I need to do all the work I can this year and next in order to really earn it," she added. "Maybe in 2028, I'll feel like I truly deserve to be in that room."

As fans wait to see who wins big at the 2027 Grammy Awards on Feb. 7, keep reading for more snubs and surprises.

Abrams failed to snag any nominations for her latest album Daughter From Hell, which she submitted for Album of the Year and Best Pop Vocal Album. Her single "Hit the Wall" was also absent from the Song of the Year, Record of the Year and Best Pop Solo Performance lists.

Abrams has previously received two nominations for Best New Artist in 2024 and Best Pop Duo Performance for "Us" which featured Taylor Swift in 2025.

While Grande picked up some surprise nominations for Best Traditional Pop Vocal Performance for "For Good" alongside Cynthia Erivo, as well as Song of the Year and Best Music Video for "hate that I made you love me," and Best Pop Vocal Album for Petal, she was snubbed for Album of the Year.

Although Kahan scored one nomination for Best Contemporary Folk Album, he was not included in the major categories like Album of the Year and Song of the Year for his hit The Great Divide.

Beyoncé is famously the most decorated Grammy-winning artist—the 35-time winner scored her 100th nomination this year— but her Best R&B Solo Performance nod for "Morning Dew (Donk)" was somewhat of a surprise considering its delayed release in celebration of B'Day's 20th anniversary in July.

This year was big for Hobert, who released her debut album Who's the Clown last year, but she failed to score a nod for Best New Artist. (Her brother Malcolm Todd was also left off the shortlist.)

That's actually not all for this much-anticipated sequel. The Devil Wears Prada 2 scored a surprise nomination for Best Compilation Soundtrack For Visual Media alongside Stranger Things season five, Wicked: For Good, The Wizard of Oz at the Sphere and Wuthering Heights.

It's been a long time coming for the first-time Grammy nominee, who scored her first nods for Best Dance/Electronic Recording for "Melatonin" as well as Best Dance Pop Recording for "Too Easy."

Swift wasn't totally snubbed by the Recording Academy—she earned nods for Record of the Year, Album of the Year, Song of the Year, Best Pop Duo Performance alongside Sabrina Carpenter, Best Song Written for a Visual Media and more. But The Life of a Showgirl was not among Best Pop Vocal Album contenders, while "I Knew It, I Knew You" was snubbed for Best Country Song and Best Country Solo Performance.

Still, it was a surprise to see "I Knew It, I Knew You" score a nomination for Song of the Year, a category introduced by Swift herself during the nomination livestream, given Swift's other hits from The Life of a Showgirl.

The hype hasn't died down, Wicked is still oh so very popular. Wicked: For Good scored two nominations including Best Song Written For Visual Media and Best Traditional Pop Vocal Performance.

Disco All The Time, Grammy Occasionally. The "Aperture" singer failed to score recognition for his latest album in any category. Styles has three Grammy wins under his belt, including Album of the Year for Harry's House in 2023.

Her comeback is far from over. The pop star received her first Grammy nominations in 16 years, racking up nods for Best Dance Pop Recording, Best Dance/Electronic Recording, Best Dance/Electronic Album and Best Pop Duo/Group Performance for "Bring Your Love" alongside Carpenter.

Although Lefty rose to massive acclaim this year for hits like "Boston," she failed to receive any recognition by The Recording Academy.

#778. Chinese graduate students are now choosing to stay closer to home

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Hong Kong is expected to have around 35,000 more students from the Chinese mainland enrolled in its higher-education institutions in 2030 than in 2025. Credit: Vernon Yuen/NurPhoto via Getty

Analysis of global higher-education trends indicates that Chinese students are increasingly choosing to stay in Asia to further their studies.

Zhao Junyi is one of many postgraduate students who are rerouting back to Asia after studying elsewhere. Originally from Beijing, Zhao started a four-year PhD programme in planetary science at the University of Hong Kong in September. He’s happy about his choice.

In Hong Kong, Zhao says, he can stay abreast of updates from China’s space programme in an English-speaking, international environment, as well as “connect with the research community and collaborate with colleagues from Europe and the United States”.

Hong Kong is a special administrative region of China and has a different education system from the Chinese mainland. Therefore, students from the Chinese mainland studying in Hong Kong are thought of as studying ‘overseas’.

Zhao obtained his bachelor’s degree in astronomy earlier this year from the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor. He says he decided against furthering his studies in the United States partly because of the federal government’s cuts to scientific funding. He didn’t go back to the Chinese mainland because only those with a master’s degree can apply for doctoral courses there, whereas Hong Kong doesn’t have such a requirement, he explains.

China’s rapid advancements in space exploration are also a massive draw. Zhao’s current supervisor is analysing lunar samples collected by China’s Chang’e-5 and Chang’e-6 space missions. For Zhao, who grew up as a fan of the Chang’e programme, it is a dream come true to learn about its progress first-hand and to potentially be a part of it himself.

“Hong Kong is so attractive in so many ways,” says Zhao, who is on a university scholarship that covers his tuition fees, rent and life expenses.

Zhao is among a growing crop of Chinese students who are seeking degrees in Asia rather than in the West.

The shift can be felt most strongly in Malaysia, Hong Kong and Macau. These are the places projected to have the fastest increase in the number of enrolled students from the Chinese mainland between 2025 and 2030, according to figures shared with Nature by London-based consultancy Quacquarelli Symonds (QS), which analyses global higher-education institutions and student mobility (see ‘Student flows’).

For the wealthy, English-speaking countries that have been popular with Chinese students for decades, the projections by QS point in the opposite direction. The United States, Australia and Canada will see the number of Chinese enrolments decrease year-on-year, with the United Kingdom holding steady. The drop in the number of students headed for the United States is projected to happen particularly quickly.

The trend shows that prospective Chinese students now consider a wider combination of factors, including how far the host country is from home and how easily they can find a job with their degree, says Alice Wei, a consultant at QS.

For Zhao, one of the most exciting things about studying in Hong Kong is that it means he can visit home easily, especially for important occasions. “I couldn’t go home for the Chinese New Year for many years when I was in the United States because it was not a public holiday there.”

The number of Chinese students studying in US universities is projected to fall by an average of 4% each year between 2025 and 2030, the sharpest drop of all countries and territories assessed.

Students from China — and other countries — are facing more restrictions during and after their time in the United States, Wei says. For example, the US federal government in July proposed putting a hard limit on the duration of visas issued to foreign students and requires them to pack up and leave within 30 days of their programmes ending. Another US proposal suggests a US$100,000 fee for international students if they intend to stay to work after graduating. Australia and Canada have also introduced tougher immigration rules for foreign students.

Australia is projected to overtake the United States as the leading study destination for Chinese students by 2030.Credit: Dr. Victor Wong / Shutterstock

Geopolitical tensions are another deterrent. US-based researchers are increasingly being scrutinized over their collaboration with Chinese partners as the United States enhances research security. For Zhao and other prospective students from China, such efforts make it harder for them to imagine a future in the United States.

“Because I am a Chinese national, it would be nearly impossible for me to participate in NASA’s research programmes,” Zhao says. NASA has blocked Chinese citizens from joining its programme out of security concerns.

Simultaneously, various factors are pulling Chinese students closer to home.

Shorter geographical distances and familiar lifestyles are two possible selling points. Malaysia, for example, is projected to see an annual rise of 13% in the number of Chinese enrolments between 2025 and 2030, the highest growth in QS’s analysis.

Malaysia’s sizeable community of people who speak Mandarin or Chinese dialects makes Chinese students feel at home in the southeast Asian country, says Ngeow Chow Bing, director of the Institute of China Studies at the University of Malaya in Kuala Lumpur. A visa-free travel policy between the two nations also means that their relatives can visit them whenever they want, he says.

It is hard to compare Chinese students in Malaysia directly with those in the West, because they study different disciplines, Ngeow says. For example, Chinese students going to the United States are more likely to pursue careers in science, technology, engineering and mathematics, but in Malaysia, the “vast majority” study social sciences and languages, he says. “Malaysia is still not yet very renowned for science and tech,” he notes.

In South Korea, the fourth fastest-growing destination on the list — with a yearly increase in enrolment rates of 8% — it is the country’s high-tech manufacturing industries that attract Chinese students, such as those for semiconductor chips, biopharmaceutical and advanced materials, says Xie Yuzhen, a Shanghai-based independent researcher who studies China’s higher-education industry. Students can gain first-hand experience in these industries owing to the close relationship between big companies and universities, Xie says.

Junsuk Rho, a materials scientist at Pohang University of Science and Technology in South Korea, has observed an influx of Chinese graduate students to the country over the past few years.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03456-7

#776. LCD Soundsystem to Headline First of Manchester’s New Platt Fields Park Concerts in 2027

The show will kick off a run of 25,000-capacity gigs planned at the venue.

LCD Soundsystem will headline Manchester’s Platt Fields Park next summer, marking the return of live music at the venue for the first time in more than 15 years. Explore LCD Soundsystem See latest videos, charts and news

The show, announced on Monday (Nov. 16) will take place on July 30 and be the first of a new series of 25,000-capacity outdoor gigs planned at the venue next year, with further headline acts set to be revealed in the coming weeks. Related Westlife Sets 2027 North America Tour: Exclusive Lily Collins Pays Tribute to Phil Collins After Rock Hall Induction Watch Olivia Dean, Kehlani, Juanes & More Revealing 2027 Grammy Nominations Here

The legendary New York band, led by James Murphy, will be joined by a slate of support acts including Mercury Prize-winning Scottish group Young Fathers, rising duo Cowboy Hunters and DJs Erol Alkan and Luke Una. Tickets will go live at 10 a.m. GMT on Nov. 20 and will be available via Plattform, where further information can be found.

The park’s last major shows took place in 2011, when the Parklife Weekender brought a host of acts to Platt Fields, including Chase & Status, Kelis, Two Door Cinema Club, Mark Ronson, Jamie xx and Skrillex, among others. The festival later moved to Heaton Park, its current home, in 2013 as it expanded.

Sam Kandel, event director and founder of promoters The Warehouse Project, said in a statement: “We’re so proud to be part of the team delivering the return of live music events to Platt Fields Park. Everyone in the city knows Platt Fields has its own unique character, shaped by its fantastic location and the diverse communities who live alongside it, and we’re planning to create some truly special moments and memories there for everyone.”

He added: “The return of LCD Soundsystem to Manchester, performing in the beautiful surrounds of Platt Fields Park, after nearly a decade away is, we think, the perfect place to start!”

The event will run as a collaboration between The Warehouse Project, Live Nation and SJM Concerts.

Councilor Shazia Butt, executive member for culture, leisure and libraries for Manchester City Council, added: “With 2027 already set to be yet another massive year of live music in the city — bringing with it huge benefits for the city’s economy, local businesses and our residents — we’re looking forward to adding to this next summer with the return once more of live music to our amazing Platt Fields Park, and to welcoming even more visitors to our fantastic city.

“We’ll be working closely with concert organizers to ensure maximum benefit for Platt Fields and for the local community from the gigs, both in the run-up to, during and after they’ve taken place, and we look forward to sharing more information on this in the coming months.”

LCD Soundsystem’s most recent full-length release arrived in the form of 2017’s American Dream, which peaked at No. 3 on the U.K.’s Official Albums Chart and became the band’s first No. 1 on the Billboard 200. The record arrived five years after the band announced its split with a farewell concert at New York’s Madison Square Garden; the group has since gone on to tour extensively, including multiple residencies at London’s Brixton Academy and a Glastonbury appearance in 2024.

More recently, Harry Styles has cited LCD Soundsystem as a major influence on his latest album, Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally, which dropped in March. In the run-up to its release, Styles revealed that seeing the band perform live helped shape both the record’s sound and his approach to performing. The connection will come full circle as the band joins Styles as special guests for the Rome dates of his Together, Together tour next year, playing two shows at the Circo Massimo on Aug. 7 and 8.

#774. Small retailers brace for 'huge hit' this holiday season as shipping costs spike

When Jenni Shields began her small business eight years ago selling handmade hair accessories, she paid $2.93 to ship an order, or close to $4 in today's dollars when adjusted for inflation.

Last year, Shields said, an average shipping label for her products cost around $4.50. But when she took a typical batch of orders to her local U.S. Postal Service office last month in Kansas City, Kansas, she was shocked to see that it was an average of nearly $6 per package.

Shields is just one of the small- and medium-sized retailers who are struggling to keep up with rising shipping costs as the price of fuel continues to trend upward.

Small business owners such as Shields are facing a difficult holiday season. Customer demand is strong, but some retailers said their profits will be dented — if not eaten up entirely — by higher shipping and other costs.

Shields said she charges her customers $6 in shipping fees, which includes roughly $1.50 to cover her packaging supplies. The dramatic upswing this year means she's no longer breaking even on her orders and instead eating the added costs, she said.

"I am losing money at this point, and I've really taken a huge hit this year," said Shields, the owner of Evie Pearl Handmade, which sells bows, quilted headbands and other accessories. "I feel like it's just been this slow increase up [in shipping costs], and I feel horrible."

The surge in fuel prices since the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran in February has driven up the cost of shipping by sea, air, rail and road.

That means higher costs across the board, including for shipping giant Amazon, which reported an 11% increase in shipping expenses in the third quarter compared with last year, to individual retailers.

Globally, air cargo is going for about $3.37 per kilogram, up 43% from a similar period a year ago, according to transportation marketplace Freightos. Judah Levine, Freightos' head of research, said in addition to higher fuel, demand for fast shipping of hardware used to build data centers is helping to boost air freight rates, even weeks before peak last-minute holiday packages take to the skies.

For businesses, that runup is going to "squeeze their margins in the near-term," said Jason Seidl, managing director and transportation analyst at TD Cowen. "Larger companies tend not to be exposed to the spot market, and they'll have what we call dedicated deals in place."

But that doesn't help smaller companies, which are walking a delicate line of not wanting to alienate customers who have enjoyed free shipping for nearly a generation.

Todd Shelton, founder of the eponymous 23-year-old New Jersey clothing company that makes high-end men's jeans, T-shirts and button-up shirts locally, said he started charging customers for return shipping this week for the first time after absorbing the higher expenses this year. The shipping is deducted from customers' refunds.

Shelton said his costs have been rising for materials, too, such as his imported Japanese denim and shirt fabric from Portugal. The company is still profitable, but the higher costs have eaten into profit margins as they stay elevated, he's considering raising prices or charging for shipping to customers, he said.

Shields said she's considering raising her shipping fees for the first time in six years to keep up with the increases.

The holiday season is one of Shields' busiest. But she said she's seen a slowdown in sales because of shipping fees.

"I can't compete with Amazon on the free shipping. I can't do that. I can't afford that," she said. "I'm seeing so much of my percentage that's supposed to come back to me and my family being put towards the shipping costs."

With no sign of fuel prices declining significantly, Shields, who runs her business out of her spare bedroom at home, said she's not sure that small businesses will be able to emerge on the other side of the holidays.

Shippers including UPS, FedEx and USPS have all instituted holiday surcharges, with prices varying by package type and lasting through the end of the season. Though that's typical during the peak holiday period each year, those charges have continued to rise over the past few years.

But even as costs everywhere climb, consumers are still spending.

According to the National Retail Federation, retail sales through the end of the year are expected to grow 4.2%, translating to total spending of $1.01 trillion. That's compared with last year's holiday sales totaling $972 billion, which was 3.1% growth.

Some of that growth is from inflation, meaning consumers are simply paying more for the same goods.

"Customers all expect to spend more this holiday, but part of why they expect to spend more is they expect things to cost more, not because they'd like to spend more or they were hoping to get more quantity of stuff," said Aaron Cheris, the global retail practice head at Bain & Company. "So what I suspect happens is that non-discretionary categories do fine, because you buy the food you were going to need to buy anyway, but then the amount of cash that's left over for [discretionary] goods is less."

Still, Cheris said it's shaping up to be a record year for shipping costs, which is putting immense pressure on smaller retailers. That means many retailers may find themselves in financial distress in the first quarter of next year as they struggle to make it through the holiday season.

He added that larger retail companies will also have to reckon with rising costs, though they may not feel those effects until later quarters because they have shipping contracts that have already been locked in and have control over their own delivery fleets.

"If anything, it benefits the scale players over the little players, but it's kind of a little bit bad for everybody," Cheris said. "I think that is the challenge."

#773. Madonna & Slayyyter Lead 2027 Dance/Electronic Grammy Nominations

The Grammy Awards are set to take place Feb. 7 in Los Angeles.

Madonna, Slayyyter, Tame Impala and Tinashe lead the nominees in the dance/electronic categories at the 2027 Grammy Awards.

Nominees were announced early on Monday (Nov. 16), setting up the race for the awards ceremony happening Feb. 7 in Los Angeles.

As widely predicted, Madonna leads the pack, with nominations in all four of the dance electronic categories. Her July album Confessions II generated nods for best dance/electronic album, best dance/electronic recording, best dance pop recording and best remixed recording.

Meanwhile, Slayyyter comes in second on the list, with her March album Wor$t Girl In America getting nods in the best dance/electronic album category along with best dance/electronic recording and best dance pop recording.
